# Wiedisync — Dev / Deploy Log

Operator-facing history of backend, deploy, and migration work on the wiedisync platform.
Newest first.

- **2026-09-06** **The bilingual feedback export, committed three weeks after it was written (no migration, dev+prod)** — `opnform-feedback-export.mjs` and its 12 unit tests had been sitting untracked in the working tree since 20.08, so the one tool that can read the scorer-course feedback as a single dataset existed on exactly one machine and on no branch. Merges the EN and DE forms into one CSV, which is only sound because the DE form was created as a translated copy that **reuses the EN field UUIDs** — the script asserts that invariant (`assertSameShape`) and refuses to emit rather than quietly aligning two different questions under one column. ⚠ Matching keys do not mean matching answers: an OpnForm select stores the option **NAME**, so the same click is "Yes" on one form and "Ja" on the other; those fold back to the EN wording via the option `id`, never a hardcoded word list, so re-wording an option in the builder does not break it. Headers are the EN labels in EN field order, per the repo-wide rule that every export is English whoever runs it. ⓘ Deployed with `scripts:deploy` — `directus/scripts/` is a separate bind-mount that `ext:deploy` does **not** reach. ⚠ eslint's `no-undef` does not cover `directus/scripts/`, so executing it is the only real gate: `node --test` 12/12 ✓, full `npm run test:scripts` 184/184 ✓.

- **2026-09-06** **The Hallenplan drew five empty hours at full scale and pushed the evening off the screen (no migration, dev+prod)** — asked as *"could we have like a 'break' between the training times so it doesn't show here for example 12 to 18 as there's nothing?"*. The grid was one linear minute→pixel map (`top = (min - baseMinute) / SLOT_MINUTES * SLOT_HEIGHT`), so an afternoon nobody books cost exactly as much vertical space as the 17:00–22:00 block that is the only part anyone reads. `timeGrid.ts` now builds a **piecewise axis**: stretches with nothing in them — on ANY day, in ANY hall — collapse to one hatched band. ⚠⚠ **The load-bearing half is the inverse, not the forward map.** `topToMinutes` is what click-to-create reads, so `axisTopToMinutes` has to be the exact inverse of `axisTimeToTop` or clicking an empty cell prefills the slot editor with the wrong time — silently, because both numbers look plausible. Pinned by a round-trip test over every 15-minute step. ⚠ **Gaps snap INWARD to whole hours** before collapsing (11:00–16:00 out of an empty 10:45–16:20), so every expanded segment still starts on the hour and the 15-minute label rows keep lining up with the hour rules; without it the grid's rules drift off its labels by a few pixels per break. ⚠ **A break is clickable and re-expands just that range.** Without it the collapse is a functional regression, not a nicety: a collapsed hour cannot be clicked to create a slot in it, and 14:00 becomes unreachable from the grid. ⚠ Found while testing: the first cut used `minutes <= seg.endMin` when locating a segment, which handed **16:00 to the collapsed 11:00–16:00 band instead of to the evening segment that begins there** — every evening slot would have been drawn at the break's y, i.e. the entire feature silently wrong in the one place it matters. `<` fixes it; the test that caught it asserts the round-trip at the boundary. ⓘ One test expectation was wrong rather than the code — asserting that a single 13:00–14:00 training keeps the whole afternoon expanded, when the right behaviour is to keep that hour and collapse the two genuinely empty stretches flanking it. Rewritten to pin that instead. Threshold is 120 minutes after snapping, so a one-hour hole between trainings is left alone. Applied to **both** views: `WeekSlotView` and the mobile `DaySlotView` share the three functions (`generateTimeLabels`/`positionSlotsMultiHall`/`topToMinutes`), and converting only one would have desynced the phone grid's clicks from its own labels. Inactive-hours shading now resolves through `axisTimeToTop` for the same reason. Gates: `npm run build` ✓, eslint 0 errors ✓, **1874** unit tests ✓ (13 new, covering collapse selection, hour snapping, re-expansion, label emission, row contiguity and the click round-trip). i18n ×5.

- **2026-09-06** **A date box one day early, but only on a device east of Zurich (no migration, dev+prod)** — reported off a screenshot as *"why does it not let me select the same day? :D"*: an event whose Start read 19.09.2026 while its End picker greyed the 19th out and offered the 20th. The End picker was right and the **box was lying**. `DatePicker` rendered `formatDateZurich(parseISO(value))` — `parseISO('2026-09-20')` builds **LOCAL** midnight and `formatDateZurich` then re-reads that instant in `Europe/Zurich`, so on a device whose offset is GREATER than Zurich's (the reporter's browser was +03:00) local midnight is still 23:00 the previous day over here, and every date field drew the day before its own value. ⚠ **Only the visible text drifted.** Everything else in the control stays on the raw `YYYY-MM-DD` string — `withinBounds`, `toDateKey`, the calendar's `disabled` test, and the `min` a sibling field passes — so the picker kept enforcing the true value while displaying a different one, which reads from the outside as "the End picker refuses the start day". ⓘ **Confirmed against the DB rather than inferred**: event 29 is `all_day`, `start_date = 2026-09-20` — the form's own weekday hint said *Sunday* under a box reading 19.09.2026 (a Saturday), and Respond by showed 14.09.2027 against a stored `2027-09-15 21:59+00`. Two fields, both exactly −1 day, is a formatter, not a data problem. ⚠⚠ **The typed-date contract was the real casualty**: `parseTypedDate`'s own doc promises that "someone retyping what they see must get back what they saw" — off by a day that is false, and retyping the displayed 19.09.2026 would have committed a start nobody chose. Fixed by formatting the **string** instead of a `Date`: `formatDateZurich('2026-09-20')` goes through `parseFlexible` (UTC midnight) and is timezone-proof. ⓘ Reproduced and verified by running the helpers under `TZ=Europe/Riga`, which reproduces the screenshot exactly (box 19.09.2026, weekday Sunday, respond-by 14.09.2027, calendar floor 2026-09-20) and returns 20.09.2026 after the fix — the bug is invisible from Switzerland, which is why it survived every date-format pass. ⓘ Grepped the rest of the app for the same round-trip: the four other `formatXZurich(new Date(...))` hits are all real instants (`new Date()`, a received timestamp, a kickoff time), which is exactly what the helper is for. Frontend-only, no migration, no `ext:deploy`. Gates: `npm run build` ✓, eslint 0 errors (76 pre-existing warnings) ✓.

- **2026-09-06** **Four icon buttons, a nowrap title, and a card that clipped rather than wrapped — plus a hall you could not delete and, when you could, one that left dangling ids (migration 353, dev+prod)** — reported off a phone screenshot: *"in events, the card on mobile overflows the buttons like edit etc."*, then *"if deleting a hall -> cascade delete"*. **(1)** The overflow was NOT the action cluster being too wide — it already had `shrink-0` and the title already had `min-w-0` + `truncate`. The bug was one level up: `EventCard`/`TrainingCard`/`GameCard` all wrap their content in `<div className="flex-1 p-3">`, and **a flex item defaults to `min-width:auto`**, so `flex-1` refuses to shrink below the row's min-content — which includes the FULL title, because `truncate` implies `white-space:nowrap`. The content box therefore grew wider than the card and the card's own `overflow-hidden` sheared the last icon off instead of the title ellipsing. `min-w-0` on all three is the actual fix, and it is the reason the title in the screenshot was fully drawn while the trash icon was cut — a narrower title would have hidden the bug, not fixed it. **(2)** On top of that, roster/edit/delete now drop to a phone-only footer row on `EventCard` (`sm:hidden`, divider spanning the card via a `-mx-3`/`px-3` pair), staying inline in the header on ≥sm so desktop is unchanged. Extracted to one `managementActions` const rendered in two places rather than duplicated markup; `null` when the viewer manages nothing, so a plain member never gets a stray divider. The cancel button deliberately stays in the header beside the "Cancelled" chip — it is a status control, and `CancelActivityButton` self-hides on `!canManage`, so gating the footer on it would have hidden it from anyone whose only right is cancelling. ⓘ **`GameCard` and `TrainingCard` did not have the visible symptom** and were left structurally alone: games already put actions on their own `justify-end` row, trainings already `flex-wrap` theirs into the bottom row. Both still got `min-w-0`, since the latent cause was identical. ⚠ **Found, not fixed, pending a decision**: `TrainingCard`'s entire bottom row is wrapped in `{!training.cancelled && …}`, so a **cancelled training has no edit, delete or roster button at all** — only the header's un-cancel. **(3)** `trg_protect_hall_delete` refused any hall holding a slot **with a team**, telling the admin to "Remove slots first" — busywork now that the halls page exists, since the slots go either way. ⚠⚠ **The veto was also incomplete in the opposite direction**: it only looked at slots that had a team, so a hall whose slots were all teamless deleted cleanly *already* and left `events.hall`, `game_scheduling_slots.hall` and `slot_claims.hall` pointing at a dead row — those three carry **no foreign key at all**. Strict where it did not need to be, absent where it did. **353** replaces it with an explicit cascade: slots (→ `hall_slots_teams` and `training_slot_skips` cascade behind them), closures, claims and scheduling slots are deleted; trainings, games and events are **kept** with the hall pointer nulled. ⚠⚠ **Deleting the slots does not delete the trainings** — `trainings_hall_slot_foreign` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so every generated training survives with its date, team and every participation row, keeping the free-text `hall_name` as the human fallback. Nothing in this cascade can destroy an RSVP or a result, and that property is exactly where the delete list was drawn. ⚠ What DOES go is the recurring training plan of every team in that hall, unrecoverably, so the guardrail moved from the DB to the dialog: the confirm now counts the rows first and names both halves ("Deleted with it: 21 hall slots, 81 closures" / "Kept, but without a hall: 486 trainings, 47 games"), and a failed count degrades to a warning rather than pretending the hall is unused. **Proven on dev in a rolled-back transaction against real data, not by reading**: deleting KWI B (21 slots, 20 junction rows, 81 closures, 625 scheduling slots) left **all 486 trainings and all 47 games alive** with `hall` nulled, and every one of the four dangling-reference probes returned 0 — then ROLLBACK, so dev carries no test data. ⓘ `db:setup-perms` deliberately NOT run: no permission row changed, and a needless re-run risks the clear-then-recreate hole that left absences unwritable on 2026-08-17. `hallInUse` was deleted rather than left orphaned — it described a veto that no longer exists — and `hallDeleteConfirm` was rewritten in all 5 locales, since "have to be moved first" became false the moment the cascade landed. Gates: `npm run build` ✓, eslint 0 errors ✓, 1861 unit tests ✓.

- **2026-09-06** **A training cancelled on a headcount taken before anyone had finished answering (no migration, dev+prod)** — the auto-cancel sibling of the tentative-sweep fix above, same root cause, fixed on request once the trade-off was priced. `auto_cancel_on_min` bounded on `respond_by::date <= CURRENT_DATE`, so the 07:00 UTC run killed a training up to a **full day before its deadline expired** — on the strength of a confirmed-count taken while the people it was counting were still entitled to answer. ⚠ It also had **no date floor at all**, so it reached the entire back-catalogue and could rewrite historical attendance — the same shape the 2026-08-08 audit fixed in the tentative sweep, still present here. Now: the deadline **INSTANT** via `effectiveDeadlineSql()` plus `date >= CURRENT_DATE`. ⚠⚠ **The honest bound is why this needed its own schedule.** On the once-daily cron a 20:00 deadline would not be acted on until 07:00 the next morning, and a team on `training_respond_by_days = 0` (a real value — "respond before it starts", DU18 Fire) would have its training cancelled *after it had been played*. Extracted to `autoCancelTrainingsUnderMin()` and given `schedule('2,32 * * * *')`, so the cancellation lands within 30 minutes of the deadline — when the answer is actually known. ⚠ Offset to :02/:32, not :00/:30, so it never races the 07:00 participation cron — which still calls the same helper first, deliberately, so a training about to be auto-cancelled cannot first decline and fine its non-responders through migration 352's sweep. Idempotent (`cancelled = false`), so the double call costs one no-op UPDATE. ⓘ **Zero blast radius today**: prod has **no** training with `auto_cancel_on_min = true` at all, and no past uncancelled under-min training for the new floor to have changed — checked before shipping, so this corrects a dormant feature rather than altering live behaviour. **Proven in a rolled-back dev transaction across five cases**: deadline 23:30 today (old cancels, new doesn't), midnight sentinel resolving to 20:00 (old cancels, new doesn't), deadline 2h past (both cancel), a past-dated training (old reaches it, floor blocks it), and a coach-only confirm against `min_participants = 1` (still cancels — `p.is_staff = false` intact). Gates: `node --check` ✓, eslint 0 ✓, 1861 unit tests ✓ incl. the `min_participants counts players only` assertion that slices this exact query out of the hook source. ⓘ **Untouched and still true**: this path is a raw knex UPDATE, so it fires no Directus hook — nobody is notified that a training auto-cancelled; the app only shows the cancelled state.

- **2026-09-06** **A recurring training could only ever come from a hall slot — and the picker still offered last season's (no migration, dev+prod)** — asked as *"let users create recurring trainings outside of the hall slots if need be"*, *"surface in admin in hall slots also the Halle collection; i need to add an halle etc. so that i can add a recurring training"*, and, off a screenshot of the picker, *"now that june is passed the 'until june' needs to be dropped"*. Three findings, one chain. **(1)** `RecurringTrainingModal` had exactly one entry point — pick a `hall_slots` row — while its single-training sibling `TrainingForm` has carried an `auto`/`manual` toggle for ages, so a team with no slot could file trainings one at a time and never as a series. Same toggle now (reusing `useSlot`/`enterManually`, already translated ×5); manual mode asks for weekday + start/end + hall and writes `hall_slot: null`. Both modes run one code path — preview, duplicate check and payload read a single series definition (`genTeamId`/`genDay`/`genStart`/`genEnd`/`genHallSlotId`) instead of reaching into `slot`. ⚠ **Duplicate protection had to change shape with it**: the slot path keys on `(team, hall_slot)`, which a slot-less series cannot, so manual keys on `(team, date, start_time)` — matched **client-side**, because a `start_time` filter would have to guess between the `HH:MM` an `<input type=time>` yields and the `HH:MM:SS` Postgres stores. The fetched rows are stamped with the team they belong to, so a team switch cannot briefly filter the preview against the previous team's trainings while the new fetch is in flight; the pre-write re-read (which the slot path already did) is the real backstop either way. ⚠ **A manual series is not a claim source**: nothing frees hall time when one of its trainings is cancelled — `trg_trainings_revoke_claims` bails on a NULL `hall_slot` — and the modal says so on screen rather than letting a coach discover it from a slot that never reappears. Both `trainings` triggers that mention `hall_slot` are NULL-safe, so nothing server-side needed touching. **(2)** Nothing in the app could create a **hall**. `halls` was Directus-admin-only, so "add a hall → add a slot → generate a series" dead-ended at step one for exactly the sport admins who own the rest of that chain. New `HallsPage` at `/admin/hallenplan/halls` + `/admin/terminplanung/halls`, reached from a **Halls** button beside **Closures** in the Hallenplan toolbar (desktop + mobile, both `HallenplanPage` and the calendar's `HallenplanView`) and from the Spielplanung settings' closed-dates panel. Name runs through `LocationCombobox`, so picking a known venue fills address + city. ⚠ **No permission row changed and none was needed** — `halls` has been in `SPORT_ADMIN_FULL_CRUD` since migration 027 and the route is `AdminRoute`; the gap was UI-only, which is why it survived every permission audit. ⚠ Deleting a hall that still has slots is refused by the `halls` trigger; that comes back as a sentence, not raw SQL. **(3)** The slot picker filtered by team and by nothing else, so **last season's Entlisberg and KWI A slots sat next to the live ones** — `[until 27.06.2026]` in the screenshot, three months dead, selectable, and able to generate exactly zero dates because every date they can offer is in the past. Now dropped when `valid_until` has passed, unless `indefinite` or open-ended; times render `20:00–22:00` instead of `20:00:00–22:00:00`. ⓘ Frontend-only: no migration, no `ext:deploy`, CF Pages builds on push. ⚠ The new key is `hallsNav`, not `halls`, because `hallenplan.halls` was already taken by a lowercase `'halls'` used inside a count string — the duplicate literal is a `tsc` error (TS1117), so this one fails loudly. Gates: `npm run build` ✓, eslint 0 errors (76 pre-existing warnings) ✓, 1861 unit tests ✓. i18n ×5 for the new `hallenplan` + `trainings` keys; `gameScheduling` ×4, since gsw carries no `closedDates*` strings and falls back.

- **2026-09-06** **The "maybe" that was declined before the deadline it was waiting on (no migration, dev+prod)** — found while building the no-response sweep next to it, then fixed on request. The `auto_decline_tentative` sweep in the daily 07:00 UTC cron bounded on `a.respond_by::date <= CURRENT_DATE`, which is **true from midnight of the deadline day onward** — so the 07:00 run flipped a member's "maybe" to "declined" hours before their deadline expired, and for a `respond_by` carrying the migration-322 **midnight sentinel** (Zurich wall time exactly `00:00:00`, meaning "no time given" → resolve to the activity's own start time) a **full day** early. ⚠⚠ There is no repair path and no way to notice: `trg_participations_clear_auto_marker` leaves no marker on this path, so an early flip is indistinguishable from a legitimate one — the same "only prevention, no repair" property the 2026-08-08 audit called out when it fixed this query's *other* two bugs (the polymorphic `aid` collapse and the missing date floor). **5 prod teams** had the feature on. Now bounded on the deadline INSTANT via `effectiveDeadlineSql()` — the same `getDeadlineDate()` mirror migration 352's sweep uses — with `astart` carried through both UNION branches (`trainings.start_time`, `games."time"`). **Proven in a rolled-back dev transaction rather than by reading**: with the cron simulated at 15:12 UTC against a deadline of 21:30 the same day, the old bound flipped the row and the new one did not; against the midnight sentinel (stored `05.09 22:00`, effective `06.09 18:00`) the old bound flipped it a day early and the new one did not; and with the deadline two hours past, the new bound still fires — so the feature is unchanged, only its timing is honest. ⓘ Zero rows were in flight on prod at deploy time (`wrongly_flipped_now = 0`), so nothing needed repairing. ⓘ **Two siblings left alone, deliberately.** The deadline REMINDER queries (`respond_by::date = tomorrow`) are day-granular by design — migration 322 derives `respond_by` at the activity's start time precisely so that `::date` lands on the right day. And the **auto-cancel-on-min** query in the same block shares the bad `::date` bound, but an instant-based fix there is not obviously better: with a once-daily cron, a team on `training_respond_by_days = 0` (a real value — DU18 Fire) would have its under-min training cancelled the morning AFTER it happened instead of the morning before. ⚠ That query also has **no date floor at all**, so it reaches the entire back-catalogue — the same shape the audit fixed here. Both flagged, neither changed without a decision on what auto-cancel should do for same-day deadlines.

- **2026-09-06** **The deadline only ever bit the people who answered (migration 352, dev+prod)** — asked as *"late sign up = no sign in after deadline si?"*, then *"also for no sign up please (= late sign up)"* and *"and auto put them not coming"*. The premise needed correcting first: `late_signin` fired **only** when a leader manually confirmed somebody past `respond_by` (`ParticipationRosterModal:770` → `IssueFineModal` prefilled). Somebody who never answered **at all** triggered nothing — no participation row, so no prompt, no fine, and a roster that counted them as undecided right up to the whistle. Ignoring the deadline is the behaviour the rule was written to price and it was the one behaviour the rule could not see. The daily participation cron (`0 7 * * *`, sibling of the `auto_decline_tentative` sweep) now writes the decline they never sent and auto-issues the fine at the team's configured tier. ⚠⚠ **`fines.auto_issued` — reserved by migration 069 with the comment "no silent server-issued path exists yet" — is now real, and the club chose it explicitly** over a coach-confirms-the-prompt variant, told that a fine is immutable once issued (`FINE_BLOCKED_UPDATE_FIELDS`) so a wrong one must be waived + reissued, not edited. It stays unforgeable: the create filter still hard-forces `auto_issued = false` for **every caller carrying an `accountability.user`**, so only system context can set it. ⚠ **Opt-in is ONE switch, per the club's "only if fine is enabled"**: the team must hold an enabled `fine_rules` row for `late_signin`. No rule → not swept, not declined, not fined; a team that has never opened the Fines panel is untouched. `FinesSettings` now says what the toggle arms, in all 5 locales, rather than letting a coach learn it from a member asking why they owe CHF 20. ⚠⚠ **The window is bounded at BOTH ends and the lower bound is the load-bearing one**: without it the first run after deploy reaches back across every activity whose deadline had ever passed and fines a whole club at once for deadlines nobody was told had teeth. 3 days, not 1, so an overnight cron failure still catches up. ⚠⚠ **`respond_by` is compared through a SQL mirror of `getDeadlineDate()`** — a Europe/Zurich wall time of exactly `00:00:00` is the "no time given" **SENTINEL** (migration 322), not a midnight deadline, and resolves to the activity's own start time else 23:59. Comparing the raw column — which the sibling tentative sweep does via `respond_by::date <= CURRENT_DATE` — fires up to a full day EARLY on every row carrying it, declining and fining people whose deadline had not arrived. ⚠ **Staff out** (`is_staff = false`) — a late sign-in is a player rule, not a coach one, the same line the roster's manual prompt draws. ⚠ **Called-up guests out**: the game branch joins `teamPeopleSql`, **NOT** `GAME_SQUAD_JOIN`, so `game_guests` never appear — doing another team a favour for one fixture does not put you on their fine ledger, and the escalation counter keys on member×team, a team they are not even on. Training guests stay in, gated by the training's own `excluded_guest_levels`, because a member who *cannot* answer must never be fined for not answering. ⚠ **Every correlation carries `atype` WITH `aid`** — `participations.activity_id` is polymorphic and the training/game id spaces overlap almost completely (both sequences start at 1); the 2026-08-08 audit found exactly that collapse in the tentative sweep, where training 137's deadline declined a maybe on GAME 137. ⚠ **The INSERT lives in a data-modifying CTE beside the candidate SELECT**, so the rows handed to the fine loop are the rows whose insert actually landed — nobody is fined for silence they didn't keep. The fine goes through `ItemsService` rather than raw knex precisely so `filter('fines.items.create')` runs `kscw_compute_fine_amount`; a rule that is enabled but has empty tiers throws `FINE_NO_RULE` and the decline still stands (the roster is honest either way), only the charge is skipped. `fines_auto_activity_unique` (partial on `auto_issued`, so leader-issued corrections stay unconstrained) is the DB-side backstop against a double charge. ⚠ **One push, not two**: the sweep names both the decline and the money, and `action('fines.items.create')` now skips its own push for auto-issued rows while still writing the bell entry so `/fines` stays one tap away. `participations.auto_declined_deadline` carries the same "system-owned row" contract as `auto_declined_by` — `trg_participations_clear_auto_marker` strips it the moment a human changes `status` — because without it the roster reads a bare "Declined" and a missed deadline is indistinguishable from a real "I can't come", which is precisely the distinction being charged for; it renders as "Declined (no response)". ⚠ Deliberately a NEW column, not a reuse of `auto_declined_by`: that one is an FK to `absences` and a deadline decline has no absence behind it. **Verified on dev in a rolled-back transaction against real data** (not by inspection): armed HU18's training 2551, the real CTE declined **13 non-responders**, staff excluded, every row carrying `auto_declined_deadline = t` / `is_staff = f`, `kscw_compute_fine_amount` quoted **CHF 10 / tier 1 / calendar_month**, and a human `UPDATE … status='confirmed'` cleared the marker on that row alone — then ROLLBACK, so dev carries no test data. ⓘ **`db:setup-perms:dev` fatals as always on keyless dev** (`custom_permission_rules_enabled is a restricted resource`, then `/items` `RESOURCE_RESTRICTED`), so the one new field on `MEMBER_PARTICIPATION_FIELDS` is **pending the prod perms run** — until then members cannot read `auto_declined_deadline` and the roster falls back to a plain "Declined" for them. ⓘ **Not verified end-to-end**: the JS half (ItemsService create → engine → notification → push) has no trigger path outside the 07:00 cron — dev's next run is the first live exercise. Gates: `npm run build` ✓, eslint 0 errors (76 pre-existing warnings) ✓, `node --check` on both extension files ✓, deployed code confirmed **by content** on the box (`sweepDeadlineNoResponses` ×2 in the hook, `autoDeclinedFined` in push-i18n) and `Extensions loaded` clean. i18n ×5 across `notifications`, `participation` and `fines`.

- **2026-09-06** **The label that promised an editor, and a generator that only knew half of "this team already plays" (no migration, dev+prod, v2.4.1)** — post-Spielplansitzung feedback. (1) v2.4.0's day panel gave a FIXTURE row real Edit/Delete buttons and a PLACEMENT row a muted "Edit in the planner" caption — an affordance that was a dead end (*"it says edit game in planner but it doesnt let it edit"*). Placements now open `PlaceGameModal` from the calendar; moving one is still remove-then-place, since (date, time, hall) IS a placement's identity. (2) `hardReject` knew a team cannot host while playing AWAY (`AWAY_GAME`) but not while already HOSTING — its comment argued a `games` home row was "not this rule's business" because it is either our own placement or a ProBasket fixture, which is backwards: both are the strongest possible reason not to offer that team another pitch. New `REJECT_CODES.HOME_GAME` covers both roads, exempting only the team's own pitch so the placement stays visible/removable. ⚠ **98 live suggestions on prod sat on a date their own team already hosted.** Also applied LIVE in the grid (`teamHostsOn` + an "Already hosting" badge), because the stored inventory only changes on a re-generation — the exact trap reported as *"my fault since not regenerating the slots"*. Suggestions only: a hand-placed second game is still allowed (junior double-headers). ⚠⚠ **Open, needs a product decision: the two roads still hold DISJOINT data on prod — 52 placements with no `games` row and 5 home `games` rows with no placement, zero overlap.** Those 52 home games are invisible to the entire club (no member calendar, no RSVP, no iCal, no website), the first of them on 19.09. Basketplan delivered 206 games last season, so bp-sync will eventually fill them — the question put to the planner is whether the agreed games are already in Basketplan (→ dedupe the two views) or not (→ a "publish to the club calendar" action plus an adoption rule so the later import does not duplicate 52 rows).

- **2026-09-03** **A basketball game could be created and never corrected — and a home one held a court nobody could see (migration 351, dev+prod, v2.4.0)** — reported by the basketball planner: *"i falsely put the games on nov 15th as away games and now i dont seem to have a way of editing them as homegames"*, plus *"adapting the time would be needed as teams know the date but not the exact time yet"*. Both are one root cause. She was not juggling three accounts; she was locked out of two children. ⚠⚠ **Not a Bolgé problem: 16 households share a contact email across 36 active members, and in EVERY ONE exactly one sibling holds the household's only login** (Galeczki, Stinson, Cataldi and Bolgé have three each) — 20 members unreachable in the app because a sibling has the account. The club's decision *"each child keeps her own member record"* is about **member rows** (roster, RSVP, fee, licence, federation data — none of which this touches); it was never about **logins**, and conflating the two is what made this look like it needed three email addresses. **348** — `households`, `household_members` (revoked, never deleted: the history of who could act for a minor IS the record) and the trigger-derived `member_guardians` the request path reads as one flat indexed lookup. ⚠ `household` is part of that unique key so two homes cannot revoke each other's grant. Both revocation paths exercised on dev: revoking a managed member drops its grant (2→1), a guardian losing her own login drops all of hers (1→0). **349** — `user_logs.acting_guardian`; without it every RSVP Nina makes for Zoé is logged as **Zoé** and Nina is invisible, since `accountability.user` by then IS the child. ⚠⚠ **BOTH audit writers stamped**: the items-API one in `kscw-hooks/audit.js` is the authoritative one (raw knex → the `user_logs.items.create` FILTER never sees those rows) plus the custom-endpoint one in `activity-log.js`; stamping one leaves half of every household's actions unattributed. **The mechanism**: a middleware at `middlewares.after` swaps `req.accountability` to the child for one request. It only ever NARROWS an already-authenticated identity, cross-checks the result with Directus's own `fetchGlobalAccess` and refuses unless `{admin:false, app:true}`, and ⚠⚠ **any throw returns 503 and never `next()`** — falling through would run the request as the GUARDIAN while the UI believes it is the child. Nothing touches the session cookie: no token minted, no `directus_sessions` row, so revocation is complete by construction. ⚠ Because the server genuinely resolves as the child, **all 109 `$CURRENT_USER` filters keep working verbatim and not one new permission rule was written** — which matters because dev is keyless, so new filtered perms could be neither written nor evaluated before prod. ⚠⚠ **Consent is structural, not procedural**: a grant may only target a member with no usable login, so **a member with her own real login can never be claimed** — verified on dev against two plain members (`member_has_own_login`). Shadow users are unloginnable through two independent gates verified in the running image (`authentication.js:85` refuses `status !== 'active'`; `auth/drivers/local.js:26` throws on `!password`) and cost no licence seat; a live `POST /auth/login` against one returned `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. ⚠ **`@directus/utils/node` does NOT exist in the container** (`@directus/` holds only `api` and `update-check`) — the three resolver imports come from `@directus/api` internals, verified importable **from the extensions directory itself**, and an upgrade that moves them throws (refusing acting) rather than over-granting. ⚠ `GUARDIAN_FORBIDDEN_CREATE` exists because the swap otherwise **silently inverts** `assertCreateOwnership`: acting makes `editor.id === affectedMemberId`, so every "self only" collection would quietly become guardian-writable. Blocked while acting: messaging (club decision — a parent administering a 12-year-old's RSVPs must not read her conversations with coaches; guard sits in `requireAuth`, the one choke point all 14 routes share, because Express matches `/kscw/*` case-insensitively and a path-prefix list is only a coarse net), password change, set-password, account deletion, household mutation (closes co-guardian revocation abuse in a custody dispute), the iCal token mint (it mints a bearer outliving revocation), poll votes, scorer delegations. ⚠ **Admins are deliberately NOT refused** — an earlier draft did, reasoning acting would be a silent no-op; wrong, the swap replaces accountability wholesale so an admin genuinely narrows to the child, and refusing only blocked the club's own admins who are also parents. Frontend: the banner is a **CONTROL, not a warning**, in a third visual language (orange-500 is already read-only impersonation, gold is already admin data scope; being Mila is this parent's NORMAL state) taking the child's stored accent — stored, not hashed from the id, so a fourth child never re-shuffles the three she has learned. ⚠⚠ `queryClient.clear()` on BOTH directions is mandatory: keys carried no identity and `placeholderData` is `keepPreviousData`, so without it one daughter's roster paints under the other's name with `isLoading === false`. ⚠⚠ **Cold start always boots as the guardian** — the last-used child is a one-tap hint, never a restored state, because a write-authority mode a PWA relaunch silently restores is the worst mode error available here. ⚠ Realtime is OFF while acting (the WS authenticates from the cookie and cannot carry the header, so it would hold the guardian's accountability and silently drop the child's frames); focus-refetch compensates. ⚠ The header rides `rest({onRequest})` only — the SDK applies it exclusively in the rest composable, never in `authentication()` (verified in 24.0.0) — so login/refresh **structurally cannot** carry it and a switch can never change whose session this is. The anti-mistake device is the child's name **inside** the RSVP labels ("Mila is coming", not "Yes"), under her thumb at the instant of decision, which beats a dialog a parent taps through blind by day two. Two device-global prefs were leaking between children and are now per-member: the IBAN nudge (dismissing for one daughter hid a real financial prompt for the other two) and the sport filter. Proven end-to-end on dev with real HTTP: `/users/me` returns Elin without the header and **Zoé's shadow user with it**, echo header present, and every negative refuses — unlinked member, unlinked ordinary member, self, garbage, negative id, messaging, iCal mint — all with ONE opaque `KSCW_ACTING_DENIED` (distinct codes would be an enumeration oracle for who holds an elevated role), against passing controls. `acting_session` audit row present with `user=563, acting_guardian=141`, throttled to one per hour. Smoke gains four acting negatives incl. the oracle check. ⚠ Smoke's 20 `/items` 403s on dev are `RESOURCE_RESTRICTED` — the keyless licence gate, not a perms regression. ⓘ **Permissions NOT reconciled on dev**: a perms run fatals while dev is keyless and dev's set is re-cloned from prod nightly; the two read grants (Sport Admin + Vorstand oversight) and nothing else are pending the prod run. **Deferred, deliberately**: E2EE identity documents for managed members (no keypair; every alternative either loses data or grants unrevocable access to a minor's passport scan), graduation at 18, and Stage 5 (push per-child tags + `?as=` deep links — without it the feature looks broken on a phone, and the push toggle currently reads browser state and so claims "on" for a child with no server row). Gates: build ✓, eslint 0 errors ✓, smoke acting checks 5/5 ✓.

Corrected check (returns INCONCLUSIVE until a sync actually runs post-migration):

```sql
WITH m AS (SELECT applied_at FROM kscw_migrations WHERE filename LIKE '336-%'),
     a AS (SELECT count(*) n FROM directus_activity, m
           WHERE collection='svrz_games' AND timestamp > m.applied_at),
     r AS (SELECT count(*) n FROM directus_revisions rv
           JOIN directus_activity ac ON ac.id=rv.activity, m
           WHERE rv.collection='svrz_games' AND ac.timestamp > m.applied_at)
SELECT CASE
  WHEN a.n = 0 THEN 'INCONCLUSIVE - no sv-sync since the migration'
  WHEN r.n = 0 THEN 'PASS - '||a.n||' writes, 0 revisions'
  ELSE 'FAIL - '||a.n||' writes produced '||r.n||' revisions; restart directus-kscw'
END FROM a, r;
```

It is `schedule('30 4 * * *')` in `kscw-hooks/src/index.js` (~line 4162) spawning `svrz-scheduling-sync.mjs` **inside** `directus-kscw`, writing through the items API with a cron access token, which is both why it produced revisions at all and why the 10:17 container restart is what arms the next run as a valid test.

- **2026-08-23** **A contact DELETED in ClubDesk is now a decision instead of a red badge (no migration, dev+prod, v1.97.0)** — asked directly: "is there a system so that contacts deleted in ClubDesk are deleted semi-automatically here?" The **departed** case (register says `Kein Mitglied` / `Ehemaliges Mitglied` / `Verstorben` **and** an Austritt date, contact still present) has had a Data Health row with a Deactivate button all along. The **deleted** case had nothing: `computeMemberSyncStatuses` called it `stale`, painted "Broken link", and the trail ended there. The member stayed active on every roster; `/clubdesk-deactivate` refused them **by construction** — its predicate needs a LIVE contact row in a departed status, so a deleted contact answers 409 `not_departed` — and the sync-up skipped them via the stale-link guard (an unknown `[Id]` hard-aborts the whole ClubDesk import). That is exactly the shape of the legacy rows this feature exists to clean up. Now `409 already_linked` unless `relink: true`, the panel names the current link up front and takes that decision in its own danger confirm, and both audit rows record `relinked_from_member`. ⚠ **The merge audit entry serialised the whole patch**, so AHV number, IBAN and birthdate landed in `user_logs` — which is **append-only by design** (its update/delete filter hooks refuse everyone), so a value written there can never be redacted. Field NAMES only now. ⚠ An **unparseable phone was used as a probe**: `normalizePhone` returns the raw input on failure (`{ok:false, value:s0}`) and `.ok` was discarded, so junk was queried against `members.phone` and two members holding the same unnormalised legacy string could match each other. ⚠ `sameEmail && sameLast && sameDob` was **unreachable** behind `surname_dob`, so an email-bearing match ranked BELOW a weaker one — and `candidates[0]` is what the list badge names. ⚠ The batch endpoint was a **serial N+1** (four queries per row, on every `/admin/anmeldungen` load); the classifier is split out of the fetching so one preloaded member set serves the page in a fixed four queries — verified live, `ANY(?)` array bindings and all. **Not changed**: every differing field still starts ticked — the explicitly chosen default, with overwrites marked apart from gap-fills and counted in the confirm. **Also surfaced, NOT fixed (pre-existing, club-wide, needs a decision)**: the generic `items.*` audit hook (`kscw-hooks/src/audit.js`) writes the **full payload** into `user_logs`, so AHV numbers and IBANs already sit in the append-only audit trail for every member/registration edit made through the items API — 2 such rows on the dev clone predate this work. Re-verified live after the fixes: batch across 15 rows, merge → 409 re-link refusal → `relink:true` 200 with `relinked_from: 195`, and the new audit rows carrying names only. 33 unit tests (was 25). ⚠ **The prod website release is GATED on `npm run ext:deploy:prod`** — the form calls `directus.kscw.ch` from every non-localhost host, where `/kscw/registration/check-duplicate` is **404 today**; it degrades gracefully (advisory catch ⇒ no block) but the gate is dead until the extension ships. **Then the feature was pointed at the club's real data (prod, same day).** All 36 registrations and all 711 members scanned pairwise on name, name+birthdate, email, phone, IBAN, AHV and near-identical spellings. **Three findings, all acted on.** ① **REG-2026-7074 → member #195 merged**: every identifying field matched exactly, and the form carried real new data — **AHV** and **IBAN**, both EMPTY on the member (he is 17, so AHV is *required* for the Swiss Volley licence) — plus `VB Schüler*in 1. Nothing links them by name (`nikolaos`.startsWith(`nikos`) is FALSE — the `l`), the emails differ (work `@vozzup` vs `@gmail`), the phones differ and the addresses differ; **only the identical IBAN caught it**, which is deliberately not a match key (families share accounts — Galeczki father/son, Ziegler sisters both do). He was HU14 coach since 05.07.2025 (`Gratis`, ClubDesk 1001125, holds the wiedisync account); on 03.08.2026 he filled the public form as `Trainer*in / HU14` under his **gmail**, the email match failed, and approval minted `#730` — `BB Erwerbstätige`, no groups, no account. ⚠⚠ **Latent cost: the 2026/27 dues run would have billed a free coach ~CHF 440** (no invoice issued yet — caught before the run). ⚠⚠ **The "everything differing" merge default is a TRAP here** — applying it would have pushed `BB Erwerbstätige` onto #537 and made the free coach a paying member; only `birthdate` (empty on #537) was taken. ⚠⚠ **And #730 was NOT inert**: on 2026-08-10 **Anja Jimenez** ordered his 2026/27 licence *against the duplicate*, so retiring it blind would have silently un-ordered a licence the club had already requested — `licence_status` + season + her attribution + timestamp were carried to #537 verbatim first. REG-2026-3046 was filed from the mother's mailbox and carried *her* number; approval copied it onto the 13-year-old and the sync-up pushed it into ClubDesk 1001306, so **the club's register was wrong too**. ⚠ Direction proved, not assumed — the snapshot post-dates the 2026-08-13 push of BOTH rows, so it settles nothing; what settles it is that the **2026-03-29 ClubDesk import created 452 members with 158 AHV numbers among them**, Christiane being one, months before Marie's July registration — and Swiss Volley licenses Christiane (RLL) while Marie has no licence category and is unknown to them. - **2026-08-18** **Accepting a ClubDesk Austritt proposal on its own returned a bare 500 (no migration, ext, dev+prod)** — Status and Austritt are ONE fact: migration 302's `members_austritt_needs_departed_status` rejects an exit date under a still-active `register_status`. The proposal queue applied the two halves **independently**, so deciding the date before its sibling status aborted the UPDATE and surfaced as `{"error":"Internal error"}` with the cause only in the container log. Hit on prod today for members **210/307/339/567** (ClubDesk exits of 17.08) — four 500s at 19:35, then self-healed once the status rows were accepted and the dates re-tried, so **no prod data repair was needed** (all 11 proposals `accepted`, all four members consistent). ⚠⚠ The two halves were never independent: `import-clubdesk-csv.mjs` only raises an `austritt` proposal when the **register** already calls the member departed (`COALESCE(cd_reg_status, register_status) IN (departed)`), so the sibling `register_status` proposal exists in **exactly** the failing cases — the accept path just wasn't using it. Fix: a batch accept applies every `register_status` row first (ordering only — no row added, dropped or reinterpreted), and a single-row accept carries the sibling's status into the **same** UPDATE, marking it accepted and logging it separately so both halves stay auditable (`decided` counts 2). ⚠ **No sibling ⇒ skip, never force**: its status half was refused (or decided in an older run), which means the two systems genuinely disagree about whether the person left — the date stays pending. ⚠ A **NULL** `register_status` is untouched: the constraint permits a date under it and NULL means "wiedisync has never been told". ⚠ The detection gate makes the reverse pairing unreachable (a non-departed `cd_reg_status` suppresses the austritt proposal), so the pre-existing register_status→active guard that clears the date never races this one. Gates: eslint no-undef ✓, `node --check` ✓; verified on dev by **reproducing the 500 first** on the pre-fix container, then re-running the identical call post-deploy — single accept 200 `{decided:2}`, batch with austritt listed first 200, lone-austritt 200 `{skipped:1}` + row still pending, NULL-status 200, reverse guard still clears. Dev fixtures removed and member 1 restored.

- **2026-08-18** **/admin/transfers was one 2494-line component and read as chaos — split into 44 files and redesigned around the worklist (no migration, dev only, not yet deployed)** — the code was never the problem: nearly every decision in it carried a written rationale, and a 7-slice behavioural-parity pass (each slice adversarially verified) confirmed **0 regressions** across the rewrite. The problem was that **six full-width blocks and up to nine paragraphs of prose stood between the `<h1>` and the first row anyone could act on** — including an amber "banner" that was secretly a **second worklist**, a 5-column table whose per-row controls (`not_needed` + `pending`) were a DIFFERENT set from the same member's row 200px below (`pending` + `done` + `not_needed` + clear), with nothing saying they were the same record. ⚠⚠ **The redundancy was structural, not cosmetic**: `blockedRows`/`probablyDoneRows` were counted in two top banners AND re-rendered as red/blue call-outs inside every affected row; sections A and C rendered the *same table with the same columns and the same `federationDisplay` labels*, so "🇮🇹 Italy" appeared twice on one page; the "needs no transfer" tally deliberately summed Swiss + settled while the Swiss half was **also** badged separately two hundred pixels away; and the federation contact bar rendered for two cohorts where `canRequest` is false by construction — a copy button and no action, on the ~483-row Swiss group. Now: one hidden-tally line, at most two alert strips that **jump** (set tab + filter) instead of restating a count, one scoped numbers bar whose chips are mutually exclusive and sum to the cohort, and the four cohorts behind `<Tabs>` so only one is ever on screen. ⚠ **Three real bugs, from 8 claims — 7 were refuted as documented deliberate design** (including "`federationBucketOf` skips the inactive guard once a federation is answered", which the `trInactive` badge and the members query's matching asymmetry both show is intended). The survivor: `linkVisPlayer`'s no-op guard compared `Number(input)` against `m.vis_player_no_manual`, which arrives as a **string** (`fetchItems` → `stringifyIds`, and the column is not in `KEEP_AS_NUMBER`) — so re-saving an unchanged VIS number always wrote, wiping `vis_manual_vis_name`, the sweep's confirmation that the hand-link is the right person. Now guarded through `normaliseVisPlayerNo`, and both columns typed `number | string | null` so tsc flags the next bare comparison. Plus: the letter footer printed "too long to prefill an email" when the real reason was **VIS lists no address for that federation** (contradicting the "no address" line 40px above it) — replaced by a three-way `buildRequestMailto`; and the manual-link warning looked the federation up with an **unnormalised** code while every other call site trims/uppercases, so a stored `' de'` printed the raw ISO instead of the FIVB code. ⚠ **`transferBucket.ts` and its test were deliberately NOT touched** — it is the only thing that decides who is on the worklist, its one-direction invariant is what the test defends, and the redesign routes around none of it. ⚠⚠ **Four things that must not be "simplified" later**, all load-bearing and all silent when broken: collapsed group bodies and inactive tabs stay **unmounted** (`{open && body}`, no `forceMount`) because the Swiss cohort is hundreds of rows each carrying a controlled input; the two `sv_vm_check` queries stay **separate** (the unfiltered one admits members, the filtered one can only confirm them); `noteDrafts` stays page-level (a controlled note writing into the row that renders it is React #301); and every hook stays above the single `if (bootLoading) return null` — a hook below it is a rules-of-hooks violation `tsc` cannot see. ⚠ Per an explicit ruling the **blocked-eligibility alarm now spans `needs` + `notNeeded`**: a member cleared off the worklist by `vmSaysSwiss` who still carries `done` + an unvalidated licence is exactly the person nobody is looking at, and fielding an unvalidated licence is sanctionable (FIVB DR Art. 11.4). Widening it also fixed the ruled-out table's licence cell rendering **without the VM evidence line the ruling was made from**. ⚠ **Caught by rendering, not by any gate** — all three gates were green before each of these: the wrapped 5-tab strip rendered ON TOP of the cohort description on a phone (the `TabsList` primitive pins `h-9` on horizontal orientation and does not grow when it wraps); both alert strips put their button beside the text, so `shrink-0` beat `min-w-0 flex-1` and the red heading squeezed into a ~170px column six lines tall; and the alert strip reused the Diagnostics table's sentence with a *smaller* number (4 vs 14, dangerous-direction vs all kinds), which reads as the page contradicting itself — now its own key in all five locales. Verified headless against 709-member prod-shaped fixtures: every tab renders, 0 console errors, 0 untranslated keys, lazy mount confirmed (Swiss 0 → 236 rows on expand), chips sum to the cohort, and **no horizontal scroll at 375px**, light and dark. Gates: `npm run build` ✓, `npm run lint` **0 errors** (80 pre-existing warnings, none in the new module), 1655 unit tests ✓ (+ new pure suites for the row-state, mailto and VIS-number derivations). **Not deployed and not on prod** — dev branch only, and the frontend ships on push.

- **2026-08-18** **Our own blocked dates can go ON the hall administration's calendar — one closure at a time, by choice (migration 328, dev; prod pending approval)** — the sync has been two-way since 2026-07 but only for **games**: `gcal-push.js` writes `games` rows with `type='home'` in a KWI hall and nothing else, so a `hall_closures` row the club creates has never been visible to the school. Found while answering "our Sperrdatum of the U20 tournament and basket bb is in the calendar, right?" — **the BB Mini-Turnier is, both VB U20 Tournament blocks (13.12.2026, 07.03.2027) are not**, and the BB one only because the Hausdienst typed it in himself on 14.08. ⚠⚠ **DEFAULT false, opt-in per closure.** That calendar is the school's; we hold write access because the club account could grant it, not because the entries are ours. A default of `true` would, on the first sync after the migration, bulk-write every closure we hold into someone else's calendar — including the ones that came FROM it (`source='gcal'`) and the city's school holidays they enter themselves; both sources are excluded in code as well, and the default is the belt to that braces. ⚠ **Duplicate suppression is DERIVED at push time**, never stored: overlap is read from the `hall_events` mirror of their calendar, because their entry can appear or vanish at any moment and a cached boolean goes stale silently — the exact failure mode this whole feature exists to fix. Verified live on dev: `BB Mini-Turnier` → `publishedThisSpan: false, duplicateOf: "Miniturnier KSCW"`; `VB U20 Tournament` → published. ⚠ **One event per (span, reason) GROUP naming the halls**, matching their convention — a KWI closure is 3 rows and 3 identical entries would be noise. The key is `sha1(span|reason)`, deliberately NOT a row id, so the edit path's delete-and-recreate keeps the same calendar event instead of orphaning one and creating another. ⚠⚠ Marker is `wiedisync=closure`, **distinct from the games' `wiedisync=game`**, so the two reconcilers can never delete each other's events; nothing without our marker is ever touched. ⚠⚠ **Our own pushed closures must be skipped on import** — the ICS carries no `extendedProperties`, and since migration 325 every `hall_event` closes the halls, so a round-trip would re-create the very closure it describes from a second source. Hence `listOwnedClosureEventIds()` runs BEFORE the import (the closure push itself must run AFTER, because dedup needs this run's mirror, so it cannot hand the ids back the way the games push does). **Fixed a bug migration 325 introduced**: `useHallenplanData` synthesises closures from `hall_events` by TITLE PATTERN, so an entry an admin had just overridden off was re-added to the Hallenplan display — the override worked everywhere except the one screen people look at; it now honours `closure_override`, and the query pins `fields:['*']` because an unlisted field reads as `undefined`, i.e. "not overridden". ⚠ The endpoint's first response shape reported the GLOBAL reconcile counts as the span's result (`created:1` while this span was skipped as a duplicate) — now `publishedThisSpan` plus a separate `reconcile` object. Actor in `user_logs`. Gates: migration applied dev, build ✓, eslint 0 errors, 12 new + 1589 unit tests ✓, refusal paths live-checked (gcal-source → 404, bad payload → 400, unauthenticated → 403), choice survives a full sync. **Prod: shipped and verified against the live calendar.** The all-day shape — untestable on dev, which is `GCAL_PUSH_DRY_RUN=true`, and a body the games push never produces — landed correctly: `DTSTART 20261213` / `DTEND 20261214` (exclusive, so it covers 13.12 only), title naming all three halls, `TRANSPARENT`. ⚠⚠ **The round-trip guard is the one that mattered and it holds**: the next sync reported `eventsCreated: 0`, `changed: false`, and `hall_events`/`hall_closures` hold **zero** rows matching `KSCW:%` — without `listOwnedClosureEventIds()` our own entry would have been re-imported and, under migration 325, re-created as a closure from a second source. Both U20 dates (13.12.2026, 07.03.2027) are now on the Hausdienst's calendar; `BB Mini-Turnier` deliberately left unflagged since he already covers it. ⚠ **Migration number 328 COLLIDED** with a parallel session's `328-email-accounts-reach.sql`. Both are applied on dev and prod and the runner is content (it keys on filename; lexical order is deterministic), so they were left alone — renaming would orphan a `kscw_migrations` row and need a manual fix on two databases.
