Cost one wrong "the token must have rotated" diagnosis; the fix is an explicit `User-Agent` header on any urllib/requests script against the KSCW API. ⚠ A pasted `\`-continuation also arrives as ONE argv entry with a leading space, so the script now strips its path argument and defaults it. **Verified as a full round-trip, not by trusting the API's `true`**: three passwords were decrypted back through the reveal endpoint and compared byte-for-byte with their `rbw` entries — identical, so `rbw` → AES-256-GCM → Postgres → decrypt → reveal holds end to end. Audit: six `update` rows with `password_set: true` plus the three `reveal` rows, and a query for plaintext in `user_logs.data` returns **0** — the log records *that* a password was set, never its value. Prod now **14 accounts, 6 with passwords, 3 broad-audience**; the other eight are boxes no password exists for or applies to (three postmasters, `dmarc@`, `waitlist@` — all new from the sweep — the two ClubDesk addresses, and `wiedisync@noreply`, an outbound SES identity with no mailbox). The cached prod admin token was deleted from the scratchpad afterwards.

- **2026-08-18** **Emails Garage, part 2: Migadu sweep live, and the page now says which password mails the whole Verein (migration 328, dev+prod)** — `MIGADU_API_USER`/`_KEY` set on both containers (recreate, not restart) and the sweep run: it found **11 mailboxes and added 5 nobody had written down** — `admin@{mail,volleyball,basketball}.kscw.ch` (postmasters), `dmarc@wiedisync.kscw.ch` (the `rua=` target) and `waitlist@basketball.kscw.ch`. That discovery IS the feature: the register was 9 rows of what someone remembered. ⚠ `kscw.ch` and `noreply.kscw.ch` answer **404** — not Migadu domains — which the sweep reports per-domain and keeps going, exactly the case that would otherwise look like a bad credential. ⚠⚠ **The one `provider` column conflated two different questions** and got both wrong for half the rows: where mail LANDS vs how it LEAVES. `spielplanung@volleyball` is a Migadu inbox AND an SES sender; calling it "migadu" hides the half that matters when you hand over the password. 328 splits it into `sends_via` + `broad_audience` + `reach_note`. ⚠⚠ **Broad audience is NOT a synonym for SES** — which is what the question looked like from outside. `kscw.ch`'s SPF is `redirect=_spf.clubdesk.com`, and ClubDesk is the club's register *and* its mass-mail tool, so `kontakt@`/`kscw@` newsletter every member **without touching AWS**; flagging "SES" as the danger marker would have marked precisely the two addresses that reach the whole Verein as harmless. Conversely most SES senders here are narrow (opponent clubs, course participants, foreign federations). Three are broad: `wiedisync@noreply` (`EMAIL_FROM`, so every transactional mail *and* the `/admin/announcements` mass path), `kontakt@`, `kscw@`. ⚠ The broadest one has **no mailbox and no password at all**, which is why reach needs its own flag instead of being inferred from "has a password". ⚠ Classified from **DNS checked on the day**, not assumed — and that check **corrects INFRA.md**: its Schreiber-era claim that `wiedisync.kscw.ch` has "no SES identity, DMARC p=quarantine" is stale (now `include:amazonses.com`, `_dmarc` `p=none`). ⚠ `broad_audience` defaults **false** so the badge means someone established the reach, never "nobody looked" — over-flagging trains people to ignore it; flipping it gets its own audit line. **Vaulting**: both `EMAIL_VAULT_KEY`s are now in Vaultwarden (prod entry already existed; dev added) and verified against the running containers — ⚠ `rbw sync` failed with a pinentry error immediately after the write (the "writes silently dead while reads hit the agent cache" trap) and succeeded on retry, so the entries were confirmed by diffing against the live `.env`, not by reading them back. ⚠ **Migration number 328 COLLIDED** with the parallel session's `328-hall-closures-push-to-gcal.sql`; both applied cleanly on both DBs and touch unrelated tables, and renaming an applied file would break the sha lock, so it stays. **NOT done**: populating the six mailbox passwords the vault holds — the auto-mode classifier blocked it twice (bulk vault read → network POST is exactly the shape that rule is for), so it needs a human to run `scratchpad/populate-garage.py`. Gates: build ✓, eslint 0 errors, 1589 unit tests ✓, sweep verified on dev before prod, badge render-checked light/dark/390px.

- **2026-08-18** **The club's mailboxes have a record now — Emails Garage, read per sport (migrations 326 + 327, dev; prod pending approval)** — a dozen mailboxes across five `.kscw.ch` subdomains and the only record of which exist and what opens them was **one person's Vaultwarden**; a volleyball admin who needed `scorer@` in Migadu webmail had to ask. `/admin/emails-garage` is that record: `AdminRoute` (`isAdmin` = admin | superuser | vb_admin | bb_admin) mirrors the endpoint's READ gate, the endpoint additionally scopes rows by sport (`vb_admin` → volleyball + club-wide, `bb_admin` the mirror, two hats accumulate) and refuses **every write** to anyone but a global admin. ⚠⚠ **`email_accounts` is deliberately NOT registered in `directus_collections`/`directus_fields`** — the opposite of the usual register-the-column rule, and the whole access-control story: an unregistered table is invisible to the items API (`/items/email_accounts` 403s for *everyone*, admins included), so the only door is the gated endpoint, which enforces the scope and audits each reveal. Registering it would hand every field to any broad `fields=*` policy and bypass the reveal log. A future migration must not add it; `SELECT count(*) FROM directus_collections WHERE collection='email_accounts'` must stay 0. ⚠ Passwords are **AES-256-GCM ciphertext** under `EMAIL_VAULT_KEY` (container env, not the DB), so a stolen dump is useless alone — which matters precisely because *displaying* them is the page's job. The **list route never selects `password_enc`**; reveal is a separate per-row call that writes `user_logs` BEFORE responding, sets `no-store`, and auto-hides after 45 s — a leaked list says which mailboxes exist, not how to read them. Missing key ⇒ the page lists everything and shows a banner, rather than 503-ing per row. ⚠⚠ Rotating the key **orphans every stored password**: GCM authenticates, so `decryptSecret` throws and the endpoint answers `vault_key_mismatch` — deliberate, because a silently wrong password would send someone to reset a mailbox that was fine. ⚠ A 404 on reveal means "not in your scope" **or** "no such row" — the same answer on purpose, so a sport admin probing ids cannot infer a basketball account exists. ⚠ The **Migadu sweep** answers only *which mailboxes exist* (Migadu never returns passwords): it deactivates rather than deletes (a vanished box is usually a renamed domain in `MIGADU_DOMAINS`, and deleting would take the password with it), touches only rows it owns, reconciles only domains that **actually answered**, and **refuses outright** when every domain failed instead of reconciling an empty list into deactivating everything. ⚠ Migadu's API is **per-domain** — no "list every mailbox" call — so a domain missing from `MIGADU_DOMAINS` is never seen, silently. **327 seeds the inventory**: 9 real addresses with purpose + section and **zero passwords** (a password in a migration is a password in git), `sport` set by intent not domain (`finance@mail` and `admin@wiedisync` are club-wide though their domains say nothing), and `wiedisync@noreply` flagged outbound-only so nobody hunts for a login that does not exist. ⚠ **Scope proved by unit test, not by promoting a real member** — the live vb_admin path was untestable without handing someone a role they should not keep, so the decision was extracted into a pure exported `scopeForRoles()`: vorstand/finance/website_admin (which reach other admin pages) get nothing here, and a non-array `members.role` fails **closed**. ⚠ `tier()` originally returned on `accountability.admin` before the member lookup, leaving `created_by_name` NULL for every admin whose Directus role carries `admin_access` — most of them. ⚠ **Layout caught only by rendering, not by the build**: an email has no spaces so `break-words` never wrapped it and the row shoved the password column off a 390px screen (primary action unreachable); `break-all` on the whole cell then chewed through the labels; and the revealed password shared a flex row with the buttons, wrapping mid-token — a password is read character by character. Verified light/dark/390px against stubbed fixtures. Env: `EMAIL_VAULT_KEY` set on dev (**prod unset**), `MIGADU_API_USER`/`_KEY` unset on both (sync button disabled and says so). ⚠ Env change needed a container **recreate**, not a restart. Gates: build ✓, eslint 0 errors, **17 new + 1577 unit tests ✓**, and every route exercised live on dev — create/reveal/patch-keeps-password/clear/duplicate-409/delete, plus 403 for a plain member and for anonymous. ⚠ `db:setup-perms:dev` fails on dev with `custom_permission_rules_enabled is a restricted resource` — the known keyless-licence state, unrelated: this change adds **zero** permission rows.

- **2026-08-18** **Every hall-administration calendar entry is a closure now — with a per-entry admin override (migration 325, dev+prod)** — the keyword test (`geschlossen|gesperrt|reserv|turnier|…`) was always one typo behind the people typing into the calendar: the Hausdienst wrote **`Halle Resveiert für Prüfung`** for 24.–25.10.2026 and `Resveiert` misses `reserv`, so wiedisync showed the hall FREE while the school had it booked for an exam. Rule inverted: **anything they put on that calendar closes the KWI halls**, and a human decides the exceptions on `/admin/hallenplan/closures`. ⚠ **Measured before flipping, not assumed** — replaying the live 2393-event feed through the old predicate: of 19 future hall-administration entries, 18 already matched and exactly **1** changed (the exam). Our own pushed games never reach the rule (dropped by event id, and by `VB ` prefix) — closing the hall for our own game would cancel the game it describes. ⚠⚠ **The floor was the real trap.** Under the keyword rule the closure floor could share the display floor (Sep 1) because barely any past entry matched; with every entry a closure, the first run created **150 closure rows** — every club game and training hand-typed onto the calendar since September, each retroactively "closing" halls for evenings long over. It cancelled **nothing** (the auto-cancel hook is bounded to `CURRENT_DATE`) and failed nothing — it just buried 3 real closures in 147 fictional ones. Closures are now managed **from today forward only**; display rows keep the season floor. Caught by reading the counter, not by a test. ⚠ **`end_date` had to exist before the override could**: a multi-day entry stored only its START date — the span lived in the ICS `DTEND` and was discarded once the closure rows were written — so nothing outside a sync run could say which days an entry covers. Now stored INCLUSIVE (the ICS DTEND is exclusive for all-day; that conversion is also why the exam reservation is 24.–25.10 and **not** 26.10 — no training was ever at risk, the earlier read of the raw DTEND was wrong). `closure_override` is tri-state on purpose — NULL automatic, `false` admin says no, `true` admin confirms — and **survives the nightly reconcile** because the upsert payload deliberately omits it (verified: override off → sync → `overriddenOff: 1`, closures stay 0, `changed: false` so no spurious digest). ⚠ Non-`false` junk fails **CLOSED** — a shut hall is a recoverable mistake, a booked hall shown free is not. `POST /kscw/admin/hall-events/:id/closure-override` reconciles immediately rather than waiting for 04:00, because the reversal IS the feature: verified round-trip on dev — switch off → `trainingsRestored: 1`, DU23-1 30.10 active again with `cancel_reason` and the marker cleared; switch back on → `trainingsCancelled: 1`. ⚠ Switching off a closure that is **not the sole cover** correctly restores nothing (04.12 is covered by both ASVZ Volleynight and a separate `Halle geschlossen` 04.–06.12) — the endpoint mirrors the delete hook's `NOT EXISTS` guard rather than trusting the single-valued `auto_cancelled_by_closure` marker. Actor recorded via `writeUserLog` (raw-knex writes bypass Directus's revision trail); `user` is NULL for the static-token identity, which has no `members` row. **UI**: its own list on the closures page, NOT a column on the closures table — a switched-off entry HAS no closure rows and would be invisible there exactly when you need to find it again. i18n ×5. ⚠ Mobile: a nowrap `24.10.2026 – 25.10.2026` is ~120px and pushed the row's only action off a 390px viewport (the table scrolls, but the primary action should not need scrolling) — the range breaks over two lines in `dd.mm.yy` below `sm`. Verified headless in both themes at 1100px and 390px against stubbed fixtures. ⚠ **`ItemsServiceFor` was written as a class and 500'd on the first real call** — `no-undef` cannot see a bad `new`, and the endpoint had no test; renamed lowercase so it never reads like a constructor again. Gates: migration applied dev+prod (145 rows backfilled, 2 `directus_fields` registered, prod identical), build ✓, eslint 0 errors, 1560 unit tests ✓, sync idempotent across two consecutive runs (`changed: false`). **Prod outcome**: `closuresCreated: 3` — exactly the exam reservation, `trainingsCancelled: 0` (it is a weekend), 12 future closure groups matching dev row for row, zero past back-fill. ⚠ The digest read `27 geändert` — that is the `end_date` backfill landing, not the Hausdienst; a one-off. ⚠⚠ **The `dev → prod` merge carried a parallel session's work** (Emails Garage + migrations 326/327, pushed to dev 14:14–14:22) to `origin/prod` before anyone chose to, and CF Pages builds the frontend on push. Caught before `db:deploy:prod`, both migrations read and approved, and shipped deliberately — but the lesson is `git log --oneline prod..dev` BEFORE merging on a tree two sessions share. ⚠ `EMAIL_VAULT_KEY` is set on dev and **NOT on prod**, so the Emails Garage lists accounts with `has_password:false` and can neither store nor reveal — the endpoint's `vaultKey()` returns null instead of throwing, so it degrades rather than 500ing (checked before deploying: a module-load throw there would have taken down every `/kscw/*` route).

- **2026-08-18** **The hall administration's calendar changes now reach a human (no migration, ext-only, dev+prod)** — the KWI calendar belongs to the **school's Hausdienst**, not to us, and the 04:00 cron absorbed everything it did in silence. A new „Halle geschlossen" writes per-hall `hall_closures` through `ItemsService`, which fires the migration-028 auto-cancel: **every training in that hall+range is cancelled**, disappearing from members' calendars with nobody in the club told why — and the reverse (a lifted reservation quietly reinstating trainings) was just as invisible. `gcal-sync` now accumulates what actually moved and mails a digest to `admin@wiedisync.kscw.ch`. ⚠⚠ **`eventsUpdated` was never a change signal** — the sync `UPDATE`s **every** feed row unconditionally every run (measured on dev: `eventsUpdated: 137` against `eventsChanged: 0`), so a naive "did anything change" check would have mailed the board a 137-line digest nightly, forever. The digest diffs the stored row **field by field** (title/date/start/end/location/all-day, normalising knex's `Date` and `'HH:MM:SS'` against the ICS parser's `'YYYY-MM-DD'`/`'HH:MM'` — compare the raw forms and every row looks changed) and a no-change night sends **nothing**. ⚠ **Affected trainings are read BEFORE the write**: `hall_closures.items.create` is a fire-and-forget `action` hook, so reading the cancelled set after `createOne` races it — the digest runs the hook's own selection (today-forward, `cancelled = false`) first. The reinstated list mirrors the delete hook's `NOT EXISTS` guard, so a training a *second* closure still covers is not reported as back on (the same overlapping-closure trap audit 2026-08-08 finding 20 fixed in the hook itself). ⚠ One calendar entry = **three** closure rows (KWI A/B/C), so closures are grouped by span+reason with the halls listed — confirmed on real data (`Turnhalle Geschlossen 04.02.2027` → A, B, C). ⚠ **Dev is suppressed** (`PUBLIC_URL` contains `directus-dev`): it is a nightly prod clone running the same cron against the same live calendar, so its digest is a duplicate of prod's addressed to real club admins; `GCAL_SYNC_NOTIFY_FORCE=1` for a deliberate test. Recipients are `GCAL_SYNC_NOTIFY_EMAILS`, **unset on both VPS** so the code default applies — no env change, no container recreate. ⚠ `??` not `||`, so a present-but-empty value **disables** rather than falling back to the club box (the `SCORER_EXAM_NOTIFY_EMAILS` lesson, pinned by a test). Mail failure is swallowed to a `warn`: it runs after the sync has committed, and a 500 here would invite a retry that rewrites every row. Bilingual DE·EN, Swiss `dd.mm.yyyy` / 24h, sections capped at 25 lines, calendar text escaped (the titles come from a feed we do not control). Gates: `npm run build` ✓, eslint `no-undef` 0 on all three edited extension files, 14 new + 1546 unit tests ✓, both new SQL statements executed against the live dev DB before deploy, and a full `gcal-sync` run on dev returned `changed: true / notified: dev-suppressed`. **Exposed but NOT fixed** (pre-existing, no live impact): `isClosureEvent` misses `Halle Resveiert für Prüfung` (24.10.2026) — the club's typo-tolerant `reserv` test does not match `resveiert`, so wiedisync shows that hall free while it is booked for an exam. That Saturday has no KWI training and both games are away, so nothing is affected today; the digest is what makes such an entry visible from now on.

This is the dev/ops narrative (migration numbers, dev + prod deploy status, internal IDs,
file paths, root-cause notes). It is deliberately distinct from:

- **CHANGELOG.md** — curated, user-facing release notes (English, semver), mirrored in `src/modules/changelog/ChangelogPage.tsx`.
- **git log** — the full commit-level detail.

At the end of a substantive backend/deploy session, append a dated entry here (one line per entry).
`CLAUDE.md → Recent dev log` keeps only the last few entries for at-a-glance context.

- **2026-08-18** **Events can un-invite the teams' guest players — one switch where a training picks tiers (migration 324, dev+prod)** — asked as *"can we also 'invite guests' y/n toggle, default yes?"* on the event form. Events had **nothing**: trainings have had `excluded_guest_levels` (a jsonb tier list) since the beginning and games have the hard club rule, but every `member_teams` row of an invited team was event audience, guest or not — the notify fan-out, auto-confirm, absence auto-decline, the deadline reminder and the RSVP gate all read the bare junction. So a Vorbereitungsturnier invited the Gastspieler who train with the team but cannot be entered on a match sheet, and the only way out was to un-invite the team and hand-pick the roster. `events.invite_guests boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true` — one boolean, because that is the question a coach actually asks; events have no per-tier semantics the way a training's Friday slot does. ⚠⚠ **"Guest" here is `member_teams.guest_level > 0`** — trains with us, may not play league games. NOT `participations.guest_count` (a member's +1s, still staff-only on events) and NOT the public signup door (`public_share_token` / `signup_url`), both untouched. The user picked this meaning out of the three explicitly. ⚠ **The rule is per MEMBER, not per roster row**: a guest on one invited team who is a **core player on another invited team stays invited**, and a personal invite via `events_members` always outranks the switch — so the escape hatch for "this one guest should come" is to name them. Someone on **none** of the invited teams (role invite, club-wide) is never touched: it is not a roster question. `IS NOT FALSE`, never `= true`, so a NULL from any pre-324 row still reads as invited. **Eight enforcement points**, all of which had to move together or the halves disagree: `eventEligibilitySql` (one helper, four absence-decline call sites), `autoConfirmEvent`, `backfillMemberAutoConfirm('event')`, the `upcoming_event` daily reminder, `assertGuestMayRsvp` (a new event branch — events are multi-team so they cannot use the single-team lookup the training/game branches share), the notify fan-out in `event-notify.js`, the unanswered-nudge audience in `broadcast-helpers.js`, and the roster modal's `excludedGuestLevels`. ⚠ **Flipping the switch off DELETES the guests' existing RSVPs** (logged with member/status/note before deletion, not restorable by flipping back) — leaving them is the documented count-drift bug: the roster modal filters excluded guests out while `ParticipationSummary` counts every participations row, so the bricks would say 8 while the list shows 6. Trainings still have this drift on an `excluded_guest_levels` edit; only events clean up. ⚠ **Excluded guests still SEE the event** — the read policy is unchanged (hiding it would mean a deep-M2M policy edit, the silent-`[]` trap) — they get the card with "Guest players are not invited to this event" where the Yes/Maybe/No buttons were, exactly like a training's excluded tier. Gated in all four RSVP surfaces: event card, detail modal, per-session sheet branch, and the calendar entry modal — the last needed three extra `fields` on the calendar's events query (`invite_guests`, `teams.teams_id`, `invited_members.members_id`), which fetched none of them. ⚠ Unrelated pre-existing gap noticed there and left alone: that same query also omits `allow_maybe` / `require_note_if_absent` / `respond_by`, so the calendar's RSVP button ignores them. The toggle renders under the team picker and only when at least one team is selected — a club-wide event has no roster to read a guest level from. **No permission change** (Member/Leader read `events` with no field list; the public policy's allow-list does not need it). Gates: `npm run build` ✓, eslint 0 errors (extension `no-undef` re-probed with a deliberate undefined identifier), 1532 unit tests incl. **9 new** pinning the per-member rule the SQL and the TS helper both have to satisfy. Shipped to prod the same session: migration 324 applied (`invite_guests boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, 0 rows not-true, `directus_fields` row present), extensions deployed from `origin/prod`, `SCHEMA.sql` re-baselined. ⚠ The dev app's items API is dead while dev runs keyless (Directus 12 licence), so the four RSVP surfaces could not be driven through HTTP there — the server side was verified by executing every changed predicate against dev's own data instead: eligibility 15 → 12 on a 15-member event with 3 guests, a synthetic two-team case confirming a guest-on-one/core-on-another keeps the invite, the cleanup DELETE returning exactly the one guest row, and the knex-generated SQL replayed with untyped binds (the `'26'` text-vs-integer cast node-postgres relies on).
- **2026-08-18** **FIVB VIS now writes `members.transfer_status` — and the sync it rides on had been a season behind since July (no migration, dev+prod)** — asked as *"can you check and put automatically done/Complete in transfers on wiedisync, when they are done"*. Two prior defects had to be fixed before the feature could do anything at all. **(1) The season was a hand-maintained constant nobody re-maintained.** `DEFAULT_SEASON = 16` = 2025/26; the cron passes no `--season`, so on 18.08.2026 `vis_transfers` held **exactly one row** — Ivo Teixeira's *previous-season* transfer — while the club's real worklist, **16 transfers for season 17 (2026/27)**, was never fetched. ⚠⚠ The failure is silent in the worst possible direction: an empty transfer list reads as *"nothing pending"*. Now resolved from `GetVolleySeasonList` and matched **by NAME** (`"2026/27"`), not by arithmetic off the number — sequential-from-2010/11 is an observation about today's data, not a contract. Rollover is **July**, not September: the 2026/27 transfers were already being worked in August with `start_on` 14.09.2026, so keying on the playing season would strand the whole summer on the season just ended. The season just ended is staged **alongside** the current one so a late completion does not vanish at the rollover; only the **current** one is ever reconciled. **(2) The table was write-only.** Nothing in `src/`, the endpoints or the hooks had ever selected from `vis_transfers` — `/admin/transfers` cross-checks Volleymanager's `licence_validated` (a downstream proxy) and never FIVB's own answer — so even a correct sync changed nothing anybody could see. **The reconciliation**: `VIS complete + NULL|pending → 'done'` (attributed `transfer_done_by_name = 'FIVB VIS'`, so the page renders *"Done on 18.08.2026 by FIVB VIS"* with no UI change), `VIS in progress + NULL → 'pending'`, `VIS in progress + 'done' → 'pending'` (revert), `'not_needed' → untouched + reported`, no live VIS row → untouched. ⚠ **"Complete" is `percent_complete = 100` OR an ended status (200/210/215/220), NOT "ended" alone** — all seven transfers the club had cleared by hand sat at status **130 / 100%** and not one had reached 200, which only arrives once the season starts; requiring it would have found **zero** to do for another month. Cancelled (239/240), refused (255) and soft-deleted rows are not evidence in **either** direction. ⚠⚠ **The revert makes VIS authoritative both ways and will fight a human** — mark somebody done while VIS shows 0% and the next nightly run puts them back. Deliberate (user's call): a `done` whose ITC has not landed asserts an eligibility the player does not have, and fielding an unvalidated licence is sanctionable (FIVB Disciplinary Regs Art. 11.4). The escape hatch for a transfer genuinely settled outside VIS is **`not_needed`**, which the sync never touches. ⚠ Matching is by **VIS player number only** — `vis_player_no_manual` (migration 312) ahead of the name-matched `vis_player_no` — and two members on one number is a **refusal**, not a coin flip; names are never used, because this column decides whether somebody may play. A VIS transfer matching no member is reported (`UNLINKED`), never dropped. ⚠ Only the current season reconciles, and **Teixeira is exactly why**: he holds 2025/26 *ended 100%* and 2026/27 *at 20%* simultaneously — reconciling off the stale table would have cleared a transfer that has barely started. **Validation is the good part**: dev's 03:00 clone predates the manual pass the user did later the same morning, so the reconciliation ran against the *pre-work* state and independently reproduced **8 of 9** of those human decisions (6 `pending → done`, Krawczyński `→ done`, Farina `→ pending`); the 9th is **Fabian Schenk**, marked `done` by hand while VIS says *submitted 0%* — the one real divergence, and on prod the **only** change a run would make today. Second run was a clean no-op. ⚠ The three unattended branches (`AMBIGUOUS`, `UNLINKED`, `CONFLICT`) were **forced on dev and observed**, then reverted — necessary because **eslint has `no-undef` off for `directus/scripts/`** (verified by probe: an undefined identifier lints clean), so `node --check` plus actually executing the branch is the only gate there. Every write also lands in `user_logs` with `user` NULL and `{"source":"vis-transfer-sync","vis_no":…,"vis_percent":…}` — a cron writing raw SQL records nothing in Directus, and the audit page would otherwise show member rows changing with no explanation (CLAUDE.md → actor capture); NULL actor is the established shape (`sv_vm_check`: 4,898 rows, all NULL). 16 new unit tests pin the whole decision table against the real 18.08 dataset. Cron needs **no change** (`vis-sync.sh` already passes no season). **Shipped to prod the same session** via `npm run scripts:deploy:prod` and run attended: staged 16+17, applied exactly **one** change — Schenk `done → pending` — and the immediate re-run was a clean no-op. Prod now reads 7 done / 9 pending / 3 not_needed. **Same session, the other half: `/admin/transfers` now SHOWS the VIS record** (dev only). The page had cross-checked Volleymanager's `licence_validated` — a downstream proxy — and never FIVB's own answer, so "Done by FIVB VIS" appeared with no visible evidence for it. The VIS row renders under the status control rather than in its own column (badge complete / NN% / cancelled / refused, the VIS reference, a progress bar, phase + start date), because the two are one question answered by two authorities and migration 237's design is to keep them comparable without conflating them; nothing renders when VIS has no row. ⚠⚠ **Rendering it against fixtures caught two bugs that would have shipped green**: `fetchItems` pipes every result through `stringifyIds` (`src/lib/api.ts`), which turns EVERY integer field into a **string** unless the name is in `KEEP_AS_NUMBER` — so `percent_complete === 100` is false for a completed transfer (every finished ITC rendered as "Transfer 100%" *in progress*), and `'60' > '100'` is TRUE, so "most advanced row" picked the LEAST advanced. tsc types both columns `number` and nothing else in the app compares them, so neither build nor lint nor tests could see it; the interface now types them `number | string` so the coercion cannot be skipped. ⚠ A finished ITC sits at code **130 ("in progress") at 100%** and only becomes 200 once the season starts, so printing VIS's literal phase gave "Transfer complete · In progress" — the phase now shows only when it agrees with the badge. ⚠ `status_label` is the sync's own English string; translated off the status CODE instead (11 keys × 5 locales) rather than printing lowercase English into every language. ⚠ Season-scoped to the highest staged season, mirroring the sync — Teixeira's row correctly shows 2026/27 at 20%, not 2025/26 ended. Because that parallel deploy shipped `origin/prod` — which by then was my pushed `cf72a758` — the extension half was already live, verified by marker rather than redeployed (`published_notified_at` present in the container's `kscw-hooks/src`, `duty-arrival-parity.test.js` on disk); re-running `ext:deploy:prod` would only have restarted Directus again. ⚠ An early marker check read `0` because it grepped `kscw-hooks/dist` — the deployed layout is `src/`, no build step; a wrong path reads exactly like a missing deploy. `db:smoke:prod` still **cannot run from lenovoserver** (the `SMOKE_TEST_TOKEN` / `DIRECTUS_PROD_USER_TOKEN_MEMBER` slot in `.env.local` is empty — open since 2026-07-11), so the manual sweep stood in: 9/9 core collections 200 (`members`, `teams`, `games`, `trainings`, `events`, `participations`, `absences`, `notifications`, `forms`), `/kscw/public/teams` 200, and **0 error-log entries for the whole deploy window**.

- **2026-08-11** **Loading-race sweep: the boot spinner lifted before the data it was supposed to be waiting for (no migration, dev+prod)** — reported as "a lot of things get loaded after the page gets loaded". The mechanism was never missing: `usePageReady` already implements ONE app-level spinner (a routed page calls `useReportPageLoading(flag)`, Layout keeps a single fullscreen spinner up over chrome **and** content until it clears). The bug is that pages report a composite that misses some of their own queries. **Real fixes, 3 pages**: (1) **HomePage** — the events query is gated `enabled: !eventIdsLoading`, so while the visible-event IDs resolve the query has **not started** and `eventsLoading` is `false`; the gate has to include the query that gates the query, or the page reveals with an empty events section that pops in. Also folded in `tickerScopeLoading` (admin → `allActiveTeamsLoading`, else `memberTeamsLoading`) so the results ticker stops re-scoping after reveal. (2) **GamesPage** — on the rankings/scoreboard tabs the reported flag narrowed to `rankingsLoading` alone, so the team filter bar arrived after the reveal; team scope is chrome on every tab and now always gates, with the active tab's data on top. (3) **AbsencesPage** — `allTeams` backs the team filter and `visibleTeams`, both painted on first render, but its `isLoading` was never captured. ⚠ **Four pages I had flagged turned out to be CORRECT** once the composite behind the reported flag was resolved — reading `useReportPageLoading(x)` without following `x` overstates the problem: `ScorerPage`'s `upcomingLoading` = `gamesLoading || membersLoading || teamsDataLoading || memberTeamsLoading`; `CalendarPage`'s `!hasLoadedOnce` is component state so it **resets per mount** (gates every visit, while correctly not re-gating when paging months); `NewsArchivePage` gates first load but not "load more"; `TeamDetail`'s uncovered queries are `canManage`-gated admin extras. ⚠⚠ **Never fold a user-toggled query into the boot gate** — `ScorerPage`'s `pastLoading` is `enabled: showPast`, and including it would blank the whole page behind the fullscreen boot spinner every time somebody clicks "show past". A disabled query reports `isLoading === false` (v5: `isPending && isFetching`), so it is safe to *include* one that is only gated on `!!user`, but not one gated on a control the user flips. Sweep: of every routed page in `App.tsx`, only `EmbedGamesPage` (renders outside `Layout`, so the gate does not apply), `FeedbackPage` and `SignUpPage` have no gate, all three correctly. ⚠ Known remaining pop-in, deliberately not fixed: `AbsencesPage`'s `TeamWeeklySection` is a child component owning its own `useTeamAbsences` + spinner, so the parent cannot gate it without lifting the hook.

- **2026-08-11** **Three prod hostnames had been frozen on an old build for ~3 releases — the Pages projects were renamed and DNS was never repointed (no migration, CF config only)** — found while verifying the v1.78.0 push, which appeared not to deploy. It had deployed perfectly; `wiedisync.kscw.ch` was simply not being served by the `wiedisync` Pages project. **A renamed CF Pages project's old `*.pages.dev` subdomain keeps resolving and keeps serving the deployment that was current at rename time** — it does not 404 and it never follows new deployments — and the rename also drops the custom-domain registration. So `kscw-wiedisync` → `wiedisync` and `kscw-spielplanung` → `wiedisync-spielplanung` left all three custom hostnames CNAME'd at frozen snapshots while CI happily deployed to the renamed projects: `GET /pages/projects/wiedisync` listed `domains: ['wiedisync.pages.dev']` only, and `GET /pages/projects/kscw-wiedisync` answered *project not found* while `kscw-wiedisync.pages.dev` still returned 200. Evidence the apex was stale by **releases**, not minutes: CSP `frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com` (missing the 2026-08-10 PDF-previewer `'self' blob:` fix) and an in-app changelog topping out at ~v1.75.x — so **v1.76.0, v1.76.1 and the entire v1.77.0 security release never reached a single member**, and neither did the PDF previewer fix that was logged as shipped. `kscw.ch` was never affected (`kscw-website` was never renamed). Fix per hostname: `POST …/pages/projects/<project>/domains` (goes `initializing` → `pending` and **stays** pending until DNS points at the project) then `PATCH …/dns_records/<id>` to `<project>.pages.dev` keeping `proxied: true` → `active` in ~1–2 min. Cut over 2026-08-11 with a DNS rollback snapshot taken first: `wiedisync.kscw.ch` → `wiedisync.pages.dev`; `spielplanung.wiedisync.kscw.ch` + `spielplanung-dev.kscw.ch` → `wiedisync-spielplanung.pages.dev`. **Zero downtime** (200 throughout); the entry chunk flip-flops old/new for a minute or two as PoPs converge — propagation, not a failed cutover. Verified after: 10/10 requests on the new bundle, all v1.78.0 markers present, CSP now carries `'self' blob:`, `assets:check:prod` 95/95, and both spielplanung hostnames on `index-BmqQpC41.js` instead of the frozen `index-Cjg6Pp5q.js`. ⚠⚠ **The lesson that matters: every "verified live" check in the last three releases was pointed at `<project>.pages.dev`, which is always correct — the custom domain was the broken thing and it is the only one members use.** ⚠ `assets:check:prod` cannot catch this; it proves internal consistency of whatever build is served, and it passed 95/95 while the apex was three releases behind. ⚠ One command separates "propagation, wait" from "detached, never clears": `npx wrangler pages project list` prints each project's custom domains — a hostname missing there is not attached. ⚠ Also corrected in INFRA.md: the 2026-08-05 note claiming `spielplanung-dev.kscw.ch` was "a second custom domain on the same project" was wrong about the mechanism (both spielplanung hostnames were CNAMEs to the frozen alias — which is the real reason their bundles md5-matched); it is true as of today, and the `spielplanung-dev` misnomer still mutates PROD data. ⚠ `CLAUDE.md → Domains` called `wiedisync.pages.dev` the dev app; it is the **prod**-branch alias (dev is `dev.wiedisync.pages.dev`), harmless for data because `api.ts` pins prod Directus by hostname.

- **2026-08-11** **Share links for events, trainings and games — the app had no per-item URLs at all (no migration, dev + prod, v1.78.0)** — asked as "could we have a sharing concept … like 'you can sign up for this, follow this link'". The blocker was not sharing: `/events`, `/trainings` and `/games` were **list-only routes**, an open detail modal was local component state, and even a notification tap resolved to the bare list (`NotificationPanel.tsx` `getNavigationPath`) — so there was no URL to paste anywhere, and no way to link a member to the item a push had just told them about. Now three routes (`/events/:eventId`, `/trainings/:trainingId`, `/games/:gameId`), a `ShareActivityButton` in each detail modal (native share sheet → clipboard fallback; an `AbortError` is a **cancel**, not a failure, so it must not fall through and toast "copied"), and notifications deep-link to the item. ⚠ **The linked item is fetched BY ID in its own query (`useDeepLinkedActivity`), never looked up in the page's list** — the list is always filtered (team chip, show-past, the games tab), so resolving a link against it breaks good links for reasons the recipient cannot see; identical in kind to the week-scoped closure list two entries down, but worse, because the sender's filters are never the recipient's. ⚠ The modal is **derived** (`selected ?? linked`), not written into state from fetched data — that is the React #310/#301 render-phase-setState trap, cf. [[react-301-render-phase-setstate]]. ⚠ **`AuthRoute` now carries the attempted path as `?next=` and `LoginPage` honours it** instead of a hardcoded `navigate('/')`: without it every link handed to somebody not already signed in **on that device** dead-ends on the home page, which is the normal case for a phone opening a link from a chat. `safeReturnPath()` is the single guard both the writer and the reader use — a second, subtly different copy is how open redirects get in — and rejects `//evil.com` (starts with `/`, so a naive "is it relative?" check passes it and the browser leaves the site), `/\evil.com`, absolute URLs and the four auth gates (login loop); 8 unit tests pin it. ⚠ **`/games/:gameId` sits behind `AuthRoute` even though `/games` is public** — the detail modal carries the RSVP roster, so the deep link must not widen what an anonymous visitor can read. ⚠ **Missing and forbidden return the SAME message**, or the link becomes an existence oracle for events a member was never invited to. ⚠⚠ **Not to be confused with `events.signup_url`**, the *guests'* door (OpnForm at forms.kscw.ch): a MEMBER who signs up through that leaves no `participations` row and the event card reads "0 going" while 40 people signed up — the two doors now sit in the same modal, deliberately labelled apart. Scope was **members-only** by decision; the non-member public page (`/e/:token` + a share token + a signups table, reusing `publicEventsScope()` and the `/f/:slug` Turnstile machinery, both of which already exist) was explicitly deferred, not forgotten. Gates: `npm run build` ✓, `npm run lint` **0 errors** (80 warnings, all pre-existing), 1288 unit on dev / 1278 on prod. ⚠ **Prod shipped as a cherry-pick (`9e126f50`), not a merge**: `origin/prod..origin/dev` still held 4 unreleased commits — `fix(bp-sync)` and the form-re-publish/duty-arrival fix (which carries **migration 305** + `kscw-hooks` + `scorer-reminders`) and `fix(dr)`'s `regenerate-baseline.mjs` — so a merge would have forced a prod schema migration and a Directus restart for a frontend-only feature. Those 4 remain on dev awaiting their own release. ⚠ **`CLAUDE.md` still calls the event-signup-forms feature "unreleased on dev" — that note is now stale**: `git diff --stat prod dev` shows `event-signup-form.js`, `EventSignupsModal.tsx` and friends **identical** on both branches. ⚠ The cherry-pick was done in a **stale `prod` worktree left by another session** under `/tmp/claude-1000/…/854bb77f-…/scratchpad/wt-prod` (it holds the branch, so `git checkout prod` in the main tree fatals) — it was clean and exactly at `origin/prod`, so it was used as-is rather than removed; the main tree never left `dev`, cf. [[lenovoserver-parallel-edits]].

Result: **ClubDesk already held the new price** (31 Erwerbstätige at 520, 101 Jugend at 320, 47 Minis at 220, 14 1. Liga at 570, 13 Lernende at 420) — the club had raised the fees in the register and wiedisync + the website were the ones lagging. Exactly **11** rows were stale. ⚠ **The claim in the entry below that “ClubDesk keeps the old numbers” was inferred from the fill-only rule and was WRONG** — true for 11 members, not 255. Measure the values, do not reason from the sync rule. An ungated “wiedisync wins” would have rewritten **124** register cells to fix 11: the other 113 are deliberate club decisions — 51 un-surcharged bases, **24 waived zeroes**, 10 rows priced ABOVE their category, 28 per-person amounts (155, 270, 280, 430, 130). So the correction goes BOTH ways. **307** flags the 11 (wiedisync wins) and **308** pins the register's amount into `fee_base_override` for the other 113 (the register wins) — because the native 2026/27 dues run prices through `feeBreakdown()`, so without it the August invoices would have gone out **CHF 19'355 over** what the register says, including a full bill to 24 people the club had zeroed. ⚠⚠ **`fee_base_override` is the BASE, ClubDesk's cell is the TOTAL** — copying the total straight in makes the engine re-add the CHF 100 surcharge on top of a number that already contains it (540 → 640). 308 therefore writes `fee_surcharge_override=false` alongside, and stores a pure guest's base **110 ABOVE** the billed amount to absorb the guest reduction (8 of the 113). Every row was verified by re-running `feeBreakdown()` with the written values — 113/113 emit the register's amount — and again against live prod after the migration: **623 members bill exactly the register, 11 deliberately +10 above a stale one, 0 disagreements**. Code: `buildPushCsv`'s Mitgliederbeitrag cell stops being unconditionally fill-only and now honours a pending push that NAMES the field, via the same `registerCell` gate as the register triple; nothing writes that change entry automatically (not the hook, not a category edit), so **only a migration can authorise an overwrite** — 3 new tests pin all three arms. ⚠ The 11 corrections have NOT reached ClubDesk yet: they ride the next sync-up a human APPROVES, and until then those 11 are skipped by the Saturday sync-down (302's contract). ⚠ **Migration-number collision**: a parallel session claimed `305` two minutes before mine and both landed on dev — renumbered mine to 307/308 and fixed forward (dev carries both filenames in `kscw_migrations`; harmless because 307 re-asserts and 308 is guarded on `fee_base_override IS NULL`, proven by re-running them). Prod shipped as a **cherry-pick** (`efb658fc`), not a merge — dev carried the parallel session's unreleased forms work — done in a DETACHED worktree because their stale `prod` worktree still holds the branch. Data-only: no perms run, no SCHEMA rebaseline. Rollback if ever needed: `fee_base_override`/`fee_surcharge_override` → NULL for the 113 IDs listed in 308, `clubdesk_push_pending=false` for the 11 in 307.

- **2026-08-10** **A password reset acted on the SESSION, not on the account it named (v1.75.1 cont., no migration, dev+prod)** — found by reading the error log, not from a report. Prod showed 31 wiedisync errors that looked like 31 failures and were **one**: member 263 at 11:20:51 — `/messaging/conversations` 401, `/finance/my-invoices` 401, ~20 item queries filtered on `member: 263` all failing "Invalid user credentials", 8 × `/auth/refresh` → 400, and `/kscw/client-error` **429**-ing on its own reporting storm. **Root cause**: `/kscw/set-password` tested `req.accountability?.user` BEFORE `token` and before `email`, and `kscwApi` sends the session cookie unless a call passes `anonymous: true` — which none of the three recovery call sites did. So for an already-signed-in member, mode 1 won, the emailed token was never read, and the password of *whatever account held the session* was changed. Proof it took mode 1: the `set-password` 200 at 11:20:46 left `password_reset_tokens` row 5 **intact** (mode 2 deletes it up front) and `email_verifications` 324-327 **untouched** (mode 3 deletes them on success) — neither single-use artifact moved. Two consequences: (a) on a shared browser, opening someone else's reset link changes YOUR password and silently discards theirs; (b) it self-destructs — `updateOne({password})` invalidates the caller's own session, so the app carried a dead login into the next page and 401'd every query. Fixed on **both** sides, either sufficient alone (so deploy order is free — unlike the schema-first rule): the endpoint now resolves **token → email → accountability** (explicit intent in the body beats the ambient session; mode 1 means "authenticated, no email, no token", which is all it was ever for), and `SetPasswordPage` / `SignUpPage` / `SetPasswordForm` send `anonymous: true` whenever they name an account — `SetPasswordForm` keeps the session only in its email-less "change my own password" shape. `SetPasswordPage` also calls `logout()` on success (mirroring what `JoinPage` already did), which is what actually stops the 401 storm. ⚠ **Verified on dev with a discriminating test, not by inspection**: with a live Bearer, `{password, token:'bogus'}` now returns `Invalid or expired token` and `{password, email:<no verified OTP>}` returns `Invalid or expired request` — under the old order BOTH would have taken mode 1 and changed the cron-service password. Same test green on prod after deploy. Mode 1 itself is unchanged-but-relocated and was NOT exercised live (testing it means actually changing a password). Also restored the one-segment `terminplanung/:token` route the portal work had **replaced** rather than supplemented — no catch-all in that block, so a pasted **volleyball** opponent link had started rendering blank. `dry_run` now defaults to **true** server-side (fail-safe: a curl omitting the field cannot blast 63 clubs). **Nothing was sent** — the only `dry_run:false` in the tree sits behind a button's `onClick`. Basketplan contact scraping ships as an **opt-in script, not in the nightly cron**, selectors marked unverified (that page has not been read with credentials). **The "missing" mailbox was a stale premise, not a bug**: `basketball@spielplanung.kscw.ch` went live ~22:00 on 04.08 and both forwarded ProBasket documents are in `scheduling_emails` (31366/31367, with attachments); the 10-min sync cron shows 0 errors in 24h. ⚠ `SCHEDULING_MAILBOX_SYNC_DAYS` unset → 60-day IMAP window, so anything sent before ~06.06.2026 is invisible until one backfill run at 365. ⚠ Migrations 278–280 are numerically **earlier** than the already-applied 281/282 (the operator committed those in parallel) — safe, since the runner filters on `!applied.has(name)` and ignores ordering, and the two sets touch disjoint tables. Idempotency proven on dev: all three re-applied under `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, and a 289-line schema snapshot diffed **empty**. Gates ✓ (build, lint 0 errors, 1015 unit, 122 scripts, `node --check`, i18n 357 keys × 5 locales with 0 missing). ⚠ Deploy is order-critical — chained `npm run deploy:*` only: 278–280 add columns the new endpoint code selects, and the `game-scheduling.js` sport filter reads the column 280 creates. **Prod sequence run 2026-08-05**: `db:snapshot:prod` → `db:migrate:prod` **standalone** (per [[migrate-silent-noop-gotcha]] — chaining it after the snapshot can print a false "up to date") applying 278/279/280 → `db:setup-perms:prod` **re-run after** the migrations so the two new-collection grants bind to tables that now exist (553 permissions, 0 errors; the reconcile printed no revokes/dedups on the second run, proving it idempotent) → `ext:deploy:prod` (`2d547534`). - **2026-08-05** **Cup fixtures were leaking into Terminplanung — a Cup R1 tie became an invite + a phantom 2nd game (dev+prod, no migration)** — reported as "D1 has Appenzeller Bären to be set but that's a cup game, no need to set up the game and in particular not 2 games". Both halves were real. The tie is SVRZ #417931 *Mobiliar Volley Cup, Runde 1, Spiel 28* (Appenzeller Bären 1 – KSC Wiedikon D1, `open`, placeholder 01.09.2026 00:00). ⚠ **`svrz_games.league_short` cannot detect a cup** — it holds the *team's* league category (`2L`), so a cup tie is byte-identical to a league game there; the competition only appears in `league_name` (`#7244 | Mobiliar Volley Cup | ♀`), which no Terminplanung reader filtered. Consequences on prod: `ensure-from-svrz` auto-minted invite **#202 "Appenzeller Bären 1"** for D1 (source `svrz`, `email_sent_at` NULL — nothing ever reached them, 0 bookings), and the card showed **2 games** for a single tie: the away leg was the real fixture, the home leg was `buildFixtureLegs`' empty-side fallback firing per-side instead of per-pairing. A first pass using `leagueCategory.name NOT LIKE '%Liga%'` **under-counted** — the real predicate found **7** cup ties for 2026, 5 of them still `open`, incl. two Züri Cup rows with an **empty `home_team_name`** (opponent not drawn yet → an invite with a blank name was queued to appear). Fixes: `excludeCupFixtures()` (`league_name !~* '(cup|pokal|coupe|coppa)'`, same net as sv-sync's `CUP_RE`, NULL spelled out because `!~*` is NULL-propagating) gates all four fixture-*discovery* reads — `opponentSvrzFixtures`, `resolveSyncedOpponents`, `import-from-svrz`, derbies; by-id lookups deliberately untouched so historical bookings still resolve. `buildFixtureLegs`' empty-leg fallback is now keyed on the whole pairing's fixtures (`oppGames`, **not** `oppBookings` — a manual opponent with only an away booking still needs its home leg, that leg is what `ManualBookingForm` offers as the home target); an empty side renders `noGameThisSide` (5 locales). Cup games still reach the member calendar via sv-sync (`/indoor/games?includeCup=true`) — this is scheduling-only. Verified on real data, not just the build: the predicate keeps 2020's 109 open league fixtures and drops only the 5 cup rows; prod `svrz-clubs` returns `clubs: []` for D1/D4/H1/H3. Invite #202 deleted on prod + the dev clone with a `NOT EXISTS(bookings)` guard — ⚠ the first attempt returned `DELETE 0` because the stored name carries a **trailing space** (`'Appenzeller Bären 1 '`, 20 chars, straight from SVRZ). Marking the other 14 as Gast would have contradicted the category they are billed under. **Scope — full reconcile:** every wiedisync-linked, non-muted member gets an explicit `Ja` or `Nein` (**707 rows**, 27 Ja / 680 Nein), not just the guests, so the column carries no ambiguity between "not a guest" and "never answered". Round-trip verified by re-previewing the same CSV after the commit: **707 "Unveränderte Kontakte (entsprechen dem aktuellen Stand in ClubDesk)"**. - **2026-07-27** **…and made it a sync instead of a snapshot — Gast joins the push + drift set (migration 244, endpoint + scripts)** — the backfill above was a one-off import, i.e. a snapshot: guest status is per-season, so it would have silently rotted at the next roster turnover with nothing to catch it. **Push side**: `'Gast'` joins `CD_PUSH_CONTACT_HEADERS`, so every UPDATE *and* CREATE row now carries it (15 contact columns / 26 create columns). New `gastCell(isGuest)` is **total** — a non-guest asserts `'Nein'` rather than sending an empty cell, which also makes the field structurally exempt from the echo-back / blank-risk machinery (there is no empty wiedisync value that could blank the register, so the guard has nothing to guard). ⚠ The flag comes from **`guestMemberIdSet`, never a bare `guest_level > 0`** — a guest on one team who is a core player on another is a full member and is billed as one by `deriveMitgliederbeitrag`, so the looser rule would have the same CSV contradict itself. `/up` now resolves `m.is_guest` **once over the whole push** (`pushMembers`) instead of only over the CREATE set, so an update row and a create row cannot be resolved against different definitions. **Drift side**: migration **244** adds `clubdesk_export.gast` (the 064 `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op on existing DBs, so a staging column needs its own ALTER — the gap `js_id`/195 and `wiedisync_id` already hit), `import-clubdesk-csv.mjs` maps `'Gast' → gast` in `HEADER_TO_COL` + `TARGET_COLS` (66 staged columns), and `computeClubdeskDrift` compares the register's cell against the live roster using **the very same `guestMemberIdSet` + `gastCell` the push uses** — a drift verdict that could disagree with the pushed cell would re-flag the member on every refresh and never converge. A member who starts or stops being a guest now surfaces as an ordinary CONFLICT the admin flags → pushes. ⚠ **Direction is one-way by design**: there is deliberately NO write-back pass into `members` — wiedisync owns guest status outright, so letting ClubDesk's copy flow back would let a stale register overwrite the live roster. The staging column exists only to answer "what does the register currently say". ⚠ `clubdesk_export` is a raw staging table, **not** a Directus collection (no `directus_fields` row, no items-API exposure), so 244 touches no permission row and `setup-permissions.mjs` is untouched. ⚠ **Until the next sync-down stages the column, `cd.gast` is NULL for all 707** → Data Health shows one *aggregated* `gast` fills line (fills are aggregated per field exactly like `sex`; per-member rows are conflicts-only and `clubdesk-sync-status` keys its `drift` verdict on conflicts, so no member is falsely marked drifted). Running a **Sync down** after deploy clears it, since the register already holds the values. **Also fixed — the summary-count bug found during the backfill's own verification**: `countFor(/(Veränderte|Geänderte) Kontakte/i)` in `clubdesk-scrape-import.mjs` matched the substring inside **"Unveränderte Kontakte (entsprechen dem aktuellen Stand in ClubDesk)"**. ClubDesk OMITS a line whose count is zero, so an import that changes nothing has no "Veränderte" line to find, matched the "Unveränderte" one instead, and reported every unchanged row as changed — the verification run printed `veraendert=707 unveraendert=707` off a dialog whose only two lines were "Insgesamt: 707" and "Unveränderte: 707". Now `/(?<!Un)(Veränderte|Geänderte) Kontakte/i`. Harmless to the up-dispatcher's gate (`scrape_ok` only needs a numeric `total` + no `error`), but the sync-up modal renders that number at an admin as "changed contacts". ⚠ The regex lives inside a `page.evaluate` closure, so it has no unit test — verified against the five label variants in a standalone node run. `gast` added to `MEMBER_FIELD_LABELS` (the sync-up modal's change chips print whatever field name the drift flag wrote — it is a drift field, not a `members` column). Gate: `build` ✓, `lint` 0 errors, `test:unit` 681 passing (+3 new push cases), `test:scripts` 75/75. ⚠ **Deploy order is schema FIRST** (`db:migrate` → `scripts:deploy` → `ext:deploy`): the endpoint selects `cd.gast`, so shipping it ahead of 244 reproduces the 2026-06-19 `column … does not exist` 500s.

- **2026-07-26** **ClubDesk data-update email — the coded fields were rendered by the member's browser, in the member's language (endpoint + frontend, no migration)** — from a screenshot of the live email: *"Federation of Origin please written properly. then why 'Schweiz'? or 'Deutschland'? these should be in EN (and for FoO → CH flag + Swiss Volley) and pushed in de to clubdesk"*. Three visible defects, one root cause. **(1) The field-label table had no `federation_of_origin` row**, so `buildChangesTable` fell through to `labels[c.field] || c.field` and printed the raw column name at a human; added in all 5 locales (+`iban`, the same gap one field over). **(2) The two sides of a row came from different places** — `old_value` was a label rendered client-side by `federationLabel()` ("🇩🇪 DVV"), `new_value` was rebuilt server-side as a German *country* name ("Schweiz") — so one row compared a federation against a country, and `sex` read `m → männlich`. **(3) `nationalitaet` compared a full list against the German primary-only mirror** (`members.nationalitaet` is the trigger-derived name of the FIRST code, migration 223), so an unchanged `DE,CH` reported as *"Deutschland, Schweiz → Deutschland"* — an email claiming a member dropped a nationality they still hold. **Fix — the coded fields travel as CODES and are rendered TWICE server-side from the same raw value**: `pushValue()` → German, ClubDesk's picklist spelling (persisted to `clubdesk_push_changes`, shown in the sync-up modal, and what the register gets — `nationalityCell()` joins `loadCountryPushNames`'s `name_de_clubdesk`, NOT the display German, or GB would preview as "Vereinigtes Königreich" against a cell holding "Großbritannien"); `displayValue(loc)` → the READER's language, re-rendered per locale bucket inside the send loop. New `kscw-endpoints/src/federations.js` owns the display side (`federationDisplay` → "🇨🇭 Swiss Volley", `countryCodesDisplay`, `countryDisplay`, `sexDisplay`, `parseCodeList`); `federationCell`/`nationalityCell` in `clubdesk-update.js` stay the push side. ⚠ **The federation maps mirror `src/utils/federations.ts` and must be added to in both** — the picker naming a body while the email names a country is exactly the bug being fixed. Country names come from `country_codes.name_de/name_en` for de/gsw/en and CLDR for fr/it (small-ICU degrades to English, not to German). ⚠ **`fedSport` had to move above the diff** — the federation is sport-specific (FIPAV vs FIP), so the `member_teams` fetch now runs before the changes are rendered. **The picker had the same hole**: `primarySport` collapses BOTH "plays two sports" AND "has no team yet" into `'both'`, and `federationName()` returns `''` without a sport — so those members were asked "which federation licensed you?" over a list of plain country names. New `federationNames()` names both bodies ("FIPAV / FIP", "Swiss Volley / Swiss Basketball") in the picker AND the email rather than neither. Frontend `clubdeskFields` now diffs codes (`serializeCountryCodes(storedNationalityCodes())` vs the selection, raw `federation_of_origin`), which is also what kills defect (3) at the source; `federationLabel()`/`formatCountryCodes`/`countryLabel` dropped from the form. The sync-up modal's change chips were showing the same raw column names — `MEMBER_FIELD_LABELS` moved out of `ExplorerMemberFields.tsx` into `memberFieldLabels.ts` (a component file exporting a constant is a `react-refresh/only-export-components` **error**, not a warning) and both surfaces read it. Separately, **fr/it locale cleanup**: 53 values were byte-identical German (`male: 'Männlich'`, `mr: 'Herr'`, `plz: 'PLZ'`, `invalidPlz`, `active: 'Aktivmitglied'`, …) — worse than absent, since a MISSING key falls back to **English** (`fallbackLng: {gsw:['de','en'], default:['en']}`) while a present German one renders German. Brand names / acronyms / true cognates (Volleyball, PDF, `#`, Saldo, Adresse-fr, Saison-fr) deliberately left. ⚠ **The bigger fr/it gap is untouched: 743 keys per locale are absent entirely** (admin 354, finance 252, + 4 whole missing namespace files) and render in English. Gate: `build` ✓, `lint` 0 errors, `test:unit` 56 files / 679 passing incl. 14 new `federations.test.js` cases + 2 push-shape cases. ⚠ **Needs `ext:deploy` to take effect** — the email fix is endpoint code; the frontend half ships on push.

- **2026-07-26** **Transfers page — Swiss Volley is a federation too, and guests are not licensed (migration 243, frontend + `vis-player-check.mjs`)** — from *"Switzerland (Swiss Volley) is also a federation with their players, so use it to group the Swiss players"* + *"guests will not have a licence so take them out"*. **(1) The `settled` bucket was doing two unrelated jobs and is now split.** `bucketOf` returned `settled` for both `'NONE'` and `'CH'`, which reduced ~483 members (migration 239 seeded CH from nationality) to a single tally with no rows, no contact and no VIS state. But **Swiss Volley IS a federation in VIS with its own player index** (`vis_federations` vis_no **189 / SUI** — it was already in the directory, seeded by 241, just never used), so the same grouping the DVV/FIPAV cohorts get is available for our own players. New `swiss` bucket → its own section under **🇨🇭 Swiss Volley**, with the VIS column and the Swiss Volley contact. `settled` now means `'NONE'` only — no federation exists to group those under. ⚠ **The "needs no transfer" pill deliberately still counts BOTH** (`active.settled + active.swiss.length`): the claim is "these many members need no transfer" and excluding the Swiss because they also appear below would make it false. ⚠ **No transfer status control and no prepared letter in the Swiss group** — the letter asks a federation to grant an ITC *to Swiss Volley*, so addressed to Swiss Volley it would ask them to transfer players they already licensed; the contact row stays, because "who do we write to about a Swiss player missing from VIS" is still a real question. ⚠ **Volleyball tab only**, same reason the letter is: VIS/`vis_federations` are FIVB's, so on the BB tab this would file Swiss basketballers under a volleyball federation behind an "In VIS" column that cannot speak to them — they stay in the tally there. ⚠ **Collapsed, and the body is UNMOUNTED while collapsed** (`open={swissOpen}` controlled + `{swissOpen && body}`, not bare `<details>`): a native `<details>` only *hides* its content, so ~483 rows × a text input would have been mounted on every page load for a table nobody opened. The header still carries the count + the in-VIS/not-found/not-checked split, so the summary reads without expanding. `renderTable(groups, withStatus: boolean)` became `renderTable(groups, mode: 'needs'|'clarify'|'swiss')` — three cohorts no longer fit a boolean. **(2) Guests are out, everywhere.** A `member_teams` row with `guest_level > 0` is somebody who trains without being licensed by the club — no licence, so no eligibility to establish, nothing to find in VIS and no transfer anyone owes; they were on a worklist that could never be worked. `sportsByMember` now builds from **non-guest** junction rows only (the same rule `buildScorerTeams` already applies to duty eligibility), so a guest-only member has no sport and drops off both tabs — while a member who is a full player on **any** team still counts as one. ⚠ Guest-only members would otherwise have been absorbed into the existing `trHiddenNoTeam` line and reported as a *data gap*; - **2026-07-25** **Indefinite absences were invisible to auto-sign-out — end_date is now a hard invariant (migration 233, dev+prod pending deploy)** — reported: *"D4 Celina Paulsson has an indefinite absence but on the training of 17.08 she is in"*, framed as *"absences we did 'not blocking' should still block participation"*. **The `blocking` flag is a red herring** — it only gates the game-scheduling availability calc (`game-scheduling.js`, `AND a.blocking IS NOT FALSE`) and a few display filters; it is referenced NOWHERE in the auto-decline path. The real bug: **`absences.end_date` is NULLABLE and every coverage evaluation keys purely on it** (`a.end_date::date >= <activity date>`) — `autoDeclineForAbsence` (bails at `if (!startDate || !endDate) return`), `applyTrainingAutoRSVP` / `games.items.create` / `events.items.create`, `reEvalActivityAutoDeclines`, the `participations.items.create` filter, and the frontend `absenceCoversActivity()` overlay — while **none consults the `indefinite` boolean**. The app forms paper over this by writing the sentinel `end_date='2099-12-31'` when *indefinite* is ticked, but any row created another way — **Directus admin UI (staff tick indefinite, leave end_date blank), raw items API, older/imported data** — lands with `end_date=NULL`, for which `NULL >= date` is never true → the member is invisible to auto-decline, and worse, when a fresh training generates inside the window `applyTrainingAutoRSVP` AUTO-CONFIRMS them (exactly Celina/17.08). **Fix keeps the existing end_date-keyed design and enforces its invariant** rather than threading `indefinite` through a dozen queries: **233** adds a `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` trigger `trg_absences_normalize_indefinite` (`indefinite IS TRUE ⇒ end_date := '2099-12-31'`, catches admin UI + API + imports + hooks — the 001-triggers pattern), backfills existing indefinite rows to the sentinel, then re-runs the migration-038 hard-override so participations wrongly left confirmed/tentative/waitlisted flip to declined (038's marker-preserving trigger keeps `auto_declined_by`; already-declined rows skipped → idempotent). Frontend `absenceCoversActivity` hardened to treat `indefinite` as open-ended and null-safe on `end_date`. ⚠ **This also makes indefinite *blocking* absences correctly block scheduling** (they silently didn't when end_date was NULL) — correct, and non-blocking indefinite absences (the injury/maternity case) still don't touch scheduling. ⚠ Deploy is **schema-first** (`db:deploy:*` before `ext:deploy:*`) though no extension code changed; the migration is the load-bearing part and the participation backfill runs inside it. Gate: `npm run build` ✓, `eslint` on touched file 0 errors, `test:unit` 130/130 in `src/utils`. ⚠ Could not verify against live DB from this session (no API/SSH creds in the clone) — root cause established from code; the backfill + trigger make it self-correcting on deploy.

Gate: build ✓, lint 0 errors, `test:unit` 655, `test:scripts` 68/68. ⚠ Deploy-order hazard flagged and currently **unreachable**: new frontend + old backend would show the claim button and 403 — but `otn1_bb`/`otn2_bb` are 0/709, so no one can hit it; extensions were deployed alongside anyway. ⚠ `ClubStatsPage` counts only OTR1/OTR2 from a backend SQL view — OTN was never counted there and still isn't (separate view change if wanted).

All 13 distinct VM values resolve through migration 224's `country_name_aliases` (**256/256 rows, 0 gaps**), so there is no silent-skip class. ⚠⚠ **`sv_vm_check` has TWO nationality columns and only one is citizenship**: `nationality` = `person.nationality.countryName` (citizenship) vs `nationality_code` = `player.nationality.iocCodeOrIsoAlpha3`, the **licence's *playing* nationality** (Swiss-equivalent status for game eligibility). They disagree BY DESIGN on prod — `Deutschland|SUI` ×5, `Italien|SUI`, `Polen|SUI` ×2, `Kolumbien|SUI` ×2 — so feeding `nationality_code` into `nationalitaet_codes` would have **relabelled foreign citizens as Swiss**. VM's code is **appended with the existing code kept FIRST**, and that ordering is the safety property rather than a stylistic choice: `members.nationalitaet` is trigger-derived from the **first** code only, so all 19 keep pushing ClubDesk the identical value and **226 writes nothing to the legal register** — verified on prod (`DE,CH`→Deutschland, `GB,CH`→**Großbritannien**, `CH,SE`→Schweiz). - **2026-07-25** **Coded multi-nationality + Federation of Origin (migrations 223 + 224, DEV ONLY — prod pending sign-off)** — from "add a new field in members called FoO? Federation of Origin? and editable via edit profile. also nationality and FoO as dropdowns rather than free text (then converted to german for clubdesk). nationality can be multiselect if needed", plus "also have this in the registration form". **`members.nationalitaet` was free-text `varchar(100)` holding an ALREADY-GERMAN ClubDesk picklist value** ("Schweiz", "Italien") — so it was untranslatable for the four non-German UI locales, single-valued, and silently breakable: two prod rows held **English** names ("Italy", "Switzerland") that ClubDesk's import drops into its *"nicht erkannte"* bucket. That is what let the nationality half of the ClubDesk push stay **completely unmodified** across four independent write paths (profile, admin explorer, down-sync, approval). Backfill resolved 381/382 and the trigger normalized the two English strays to `Italien`/`Schweiz` as a side effect. **224 fixes forward** on the trap the 223 dev run exposed via that one unresolved row: **ClubDesk's picklist says "Großbritannien" where the country list (from kscw-website, which seeded the picklist) says "Vereinigtes Königreich"** — so a single canonical German name per country is not enough to *parse*, and pushing the display name would land the row in "nicht erkannte". `country_codes.name_de_clubdesk` is now the wire format (identical for 195/196) and a **337-row `country_name_aliases`** table absorbs every other spelling (`USA`, `Holland`, `England`, `Weissrussland`, `Tschechische Republik`, …). ⚠ 7 of the 196 German names also differ from `Intl.DisplayNames`/CLDR (Botswana vs Botsuana, Moldau vs Republik Moldau, Kap Verde vs Cabo Verde …) — **the backend reads `country_codes` from Postgres and must never substitute Intl**; the frontend uses Intl only for *display* labels. **ClubDesk's "Federation of Origin" is a TEXT field** (confirmed with the user), so the pushed `'Keiner'` sentinel and any country name are safe — had it been a picklist, every pushed name would have needed to exist as an option. ⚠ **The echo-back could NOT ride on `federation_of_origin` itself**: wiedisync stores a CODE under a CHECK constraint while ClubDesk's cell is a German string, so assigning ClubDesk's value back onto that field would fail the code lookup and emit an **empty** cell — precisely the blanking the echo exists to prevent. The echo therefore lands in a transient `m.federation_of_origin_cd` that `buildPushCsv` uses verbatim when the member hasn't answered. Country→German map loaded **once per push/drift run**, never per row. **Fixed a pre-existing gap in passing**: `registrations.nationalitaet_code` (migration 161) was **never propagated to `members`**, so approval silently dropped the ISO code — the member-side display had been falling back to fuzzy name matching ever since. **FIBA treats a dual national holding Swiss nationality as Swiss**, so the basketball required-document gate resolves **"CH if any"** through one shared `fibaNatCode()` (`bb-docs.js`) at all three backend enforcement points (registration create, doc-status, approval gate) plus a frontend mirror in `AnmeldungenPage` and `bbNatCode()` in the public form — ⚠ **the form and the server MUST agree**, or the applicant sees a shorter document list than the server enforces and the submission is rejected *after* every upload. The ClubDesk CSV builders deliberately do **NOT** get this rule: ClubDesk's `Nationalität` is single-valued and holds the *primary* nationality, so forcing `Schweiz` for a CH/IT who listed IT first would file wrong data in the legal register. **Permissions — the subtle one**: `nationalitaet` was removed from `MEMBER_EDITABLE_FIELDS` (the DB owns it now), but ⚠ **`MEMBER_OWN_READABLE` and `LEADER_TEAM_MEMBER_FIELDS` both DERIVE from that list**, so the removal would have silently revoked own-read and coach-read too. It moved into a new `MEMBER_DERIVED_READ_FIELDS` folded into both — **not** into `MEMBER_VISIBLE_FIELDS`, which is what every member reads about every *other* member and which migration 024 deliberately keeps free of the `adresse`/`birthdate` PII tier nationality belongs to; putting it there to preserve own-read would have made nationality club-wide readable as a side effect of losing a *write* grant. Net: own-read unchanged, coach/TR read unchanged, finance widened by the two new columns, member write revoked. All three columns added to `REDACTED_FIELDS.members` in `audit.js`. **Public form (kscw-website)**: nationality became a multi-select with removable chips (selection order preserved and meaningful), a Federation-of-origin combobox added reusing the existing `.nationality-*` CSS wholesale (class-based, so zero new styles), both new values submitted, script cache-buster bumped `3.9.0`→`3.10.0`. ⚠ The design deliberately avoided touching `bbDocSet`/`updateBBDocs` because the user had **live WIP refactoring exactly those functions** (Freibrief waivers, `bb_recent_licence`, U12 exemption) — only the two `natCode` expressions changed. That WIP was stashed and re-popped mid-session and the merge landed clean (their 5-arg `bbDocSet` + our `bbNatCode()` at both call sites, no conflict markers). ⚠ **kscw-website was left UNCOMMITTED on purpose**: on re-pop the index held their in-flight `admin.astro` / `club/feedback.astro` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `package.json` / PDF-deletion work mixed with ours, so committing would have swept up unrelated changes. **Verification**: `npm run build` green, `npm run lint` 0 errors (91 pre-existing `data ?? - **2026-07-10** **Scorer-assign upload: survive a stale exceljs chunk** — user report: the "Upload corrected" on `/admin/scorer-assign` "does not work" (red error). Traced end-to-end with the user's actual file (`260710_kscw_scorer_assignment_vb_2026-27.xlsx`): the file is a clean 80-row export, and the upload parser applies **80/80** against live prod data (0 unmatched, 0 unknown teams) — so it's **not** a data/parse bug. The only throwable op in `handleUploadXlsx` is `await import('exceljs')` (a **930 kB lazy chunk** whose hash rotates every deploy); a tab left open across a deploy gets the CF Pages SPA fallback for the now-missing chunk → import throws → the **bare `catch` swallowed it into "Could not read the file"** and skipped the app-wide `maybeReloadOnStaleChunk` recovery every other lazy export uses (download worked earlier because its chunk was still cached — the download/upload asymmetry). Fix: import failure → `maybeReloadOnStaleChunk()` hard-reload to the current bundle (falls back to a new `uploadStale` "app updated, refresh" message if reload is on cooldown); genuine parse failures → `captureApiError()` (were silently discarded); + a `uploadNotReady` guard for the race where the localStorage-restored Upload button appears before the season's games finish loading (previously a confusing "no matches"). New i18n `uploadNotReady`/`uploadStale` ×5. Frontend-only, no schema/ext; build+eslint green. **dev+prod** (dev 2908cdbe, prod cherry-pick 4724355d).
- **2026-07-10** **CF Pages CSS-breaks-on-deploy poison fixed + repo/docs cleanup** — user hit "Refused to apply style from `.../assets/index-CIAnGfI5.css` because its MIME type ('text/html')" → whole app unstyled, broken in **every** browser, cleared only by a CF dashboard "Purge Everything". **Root cause**: CF Pages serves the SPA `index.html` fallback (`200 text/html`) for a *missing* `/assets/<hash>` (not-yet-propagated / reused hash during a deploy), and `public/_headers` stamps `Cache-Control: immutable` on everything matching `/assets/*` **by URL** — so the CF **edge** caches that `200 text/html immutable` under the real asset URL and serves it to all clients until a manual purge; `_headers` can't tell a real asset from a miss (same URL). **Dead ends (both tested on dev)**: `_redirects` can't return a `404` status (rule silently dropped → poison returns); a `public/404.html` makes CF serve it for ALL not-found → every SPA deep link 404s. **Fix**: Pages Function `functions/assets/[[path]].js` — `env.ASSETS.fetch()` the request; a 404 or `text/html` result (asset missing) → real `404` + `Cache-Control: no-store`; else pass the real asset through untouched (keeps immutable, still edge-cached). `public/_redirects` keeps only `/* /index.html 200`. **Verified on prod** `wiedisync.kscw.ch`: misses → `404 no-store`, real `index-CIAnGfI5.css` → `200 text/css immutable`, SPA routes → `200`. Documented in `INFRA.md → Troubleshooting`. Frontend-only, no schema/ext. **dev+prod** (dev c8020fce, prod merge 3614d834). **Cleanup same session**: purged the CF Pages deployment backlog (wiedisync had 600+; kept newest 5 + live prod on both `wiedisync` and `kscw-website`); pruned merged local `security-fixes` branch + `git gc` (73M→20M) on lenovoserver; shrank the large tracked `.md` docs by archiving historical content into `-archive.md` siblings (DEVLOG 240K→146K, IMPROVEMENTS 123K→3.7K, SECURITY 73K→18K, CHANGELOG 34K→14K, PERMISSIONS 38K→32K; INFRA shrunk locally into gitignored `INFRA-archive.md`, `.gitignore` `INFRA.md`→`INFRA*.md` so no infra secrets are committed).

- **2026-07-09** **Mute cosmetic "game updated" notification spam (migration 199)** — `trg_games_notify` fired a "Game updated: … on DD.MM.YY" push to a team's WHOLE roster on every non-completion/cancellation `games` UPDATE. sv-sync rewrites a game row whenever any of its `COMPARE_FIELDS` drift — which includes `referees_json`, `sets_json`, `league`, `round`, and in-progress scores — so the SV feed reshuffling referee assignments / partial set data between syncs re-notified the *same* fixture (H3 vs Voléro 02.10.26, H3 vs RTG 18.12.26, …) every few hours (user-reported: "why still updating?").
